The class, in one sentence: the run's own bookkeeping — the lock record, the lock-left sentence, the progress file, the pace files — is written with the same must-succeed write as the pull's data and is never classified, so its failure decides the run's outcome (a raw stack where a refusal belongs, a live pull stopped mid-way, a finished pull's snapshot left unwritten) or goes unsaid (a lock left with no word), where it should either refuse cleanly (the lock) or be said once and change nothing (the rest).
Instances (read in the code at main 4338b6c; only (a) has been measured live):
    (a) F-563 — doc-lib.mjs acquireFileLock record(): writeFileAtomicSync renames over refresh.lock; a handle that forbids rename, held past withWindowsFsRetry's ten tries (25 to 225 ms, about 1.1 s in all), throws EPERM out of the refresh before any call — exit 1, a stack, no JSON summary, so the skill's exit-1 branch has no `error` to relay. Measured once (VALIDATION § R15 R2, a deliberate PowerShell handle); a re-run cleared it.
    (b) F-565 (1) — dashboard.mjs releasedWith(): a non-refusal error is returned unchanged, so a crash while the lock cannot be removed prints the stack and never says the lock was left (F-557 says it on refusals only).
    (c) F-565 (2) — manifest.mjs sayLockLeft: the knowledge-base manifest lock's lock-left line is written from the process 'exit' handler, where a piped stderr on Windows is asynchronous and the line can be dropped.
    (d) F-575 review item (1) — engagement.mjs progressTick: progress.json is rewritten in place (a rename over the existing file) at every tenth made call or a minute of silence, inside the pull loop, with no catch; a handle held past the retry throws out of runUnit and stops a live pull mid-way (resumable, a stack, no summary).
    (e) F-575 review item (2) — dashboard.mjs verbRefresh: writePace (the knowledge base's engagement-pace.json and the dashboard's pace.json, both renames over existing files) runs right after the pull and before its status check, the snapshot and the pages, unguarded, so a failed pace write fails a refresh whose calls all succeeded; a re-run reuses the calls and finishes.
    Test hygiene that rides along (F-565): test/dashboard.mjs's F-557 arm removes its icacls denies on the happy path only, so a throw in between leaves an undeletable temp folder.
Siblings to classify at kickoff (the census of every file write in engagement.mjs and dashboard.mjs, 2026-10-21; unmeasured): engagement.mjs's closing status.json (conclude(), rewritten over) and the kb-steps.json cache (two sites) are bookkeeping by the same test. ONE home in doc-lib, beside writeFileAtomicSync and the lock primitive: writeBookkeepingSync(path, data, what) writes atomically and hands a failure back as {path, what, why, text}, never throws; acquireFileLock's record() writes through it and returns the failure for the caller's one-line refusal; sayLineSync writes a line to fd 2 synchronously. Every bookkeeping site calls the home and keeps no try/catch of its own: (a) the dashboard's takeLock record — a refusal "the refresh lock of "<slug>" could not be recorded (EPERM): a handle on <path> (a scanner, a sync client, an editor) forbids the write — run the line again once it is gone", lockRecord on the summary, the lock then released or said left by the verb's one release path (releasedWith), exit 1, one JSON line, no stack; (b) attachSaid, the one attacher: a lock left on a CRASH is said on stderr synchronously beside the stack ("dashboard.mjs: the refresh lock could not be removed at the end …"), on a refusal appended, on a summary carried; (c) manifest.mjs's sayLockLeft writes through sayLineSync, so the 'exit' and signal handlers' line cannot be dropped on a piped stderr; (d) progressTick writes progress.json through the home and a failure is said ONCE (onNote, the dashboard's "pull bookkeeping: …" line, and bookkeepingLeft on the summary), the pull going on; (e) writePaceFile returns {written, left}, verbRefresh says each left once and goes on to its snapshot and pages, the summary's pace null when the dashboard's own file was not written, a stop's refusal carrying bookkeepingLeft too. The line between bookkeeping and DATA, measured in loadRun rather than assumed: status.json and kb-steps.json are READ by the reduce (it refuses without the first and silently loses the schedules without the second), so both keep the must-succeed write with run.json, plan.json, the gap lists, the call files, the snapshot, the store, the pages and the state file — the kickoff census's two "siblings to classify" are data by that test. Sibling case the tester did not list: a stale progress record that cannot be REMOVED at a resume (a folder at its path) stops nothing; the first tick's write fails the same way and is said once. Test hygiene (F-565's ride-along): the F-557 arm's denies come off at process exit, however the suite ends. Reported: 2026-10-24 (builder)

## F-584 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-24 (tester)
Severity: normal — the pre-push hook is the only gate before a string reaches GitHub, and it passes a push whose commits carry one whenever the checkout the hook runs in is clean (F-583's own tier reasoning: the failure mode is an org identifier on a public branch)
Source: F-583 acceptance round @ hb-20261024-01, a sibling of arm F (the hook arm)
What: dev/hooks/pre-push prints "instance-data gate on <remote_ref>" for each pushed ref, but then runs node build/check-instance-data.mjs in the checkout it was invoked from, which scans that checkout's index (git ls-files), never the tree of the commit being pushed. A push of any ref other than the checked-out one (git push origin <other-branch>, a push of several refs, a push of a branch that a second worktree has checked out) is gated by whatever the current checkout holds, under a line that names the pushed ref. The bus header's Hooks: line ("runs check-instance-data on EVERY ref (F-423)") and F-424's "weaker run than the tree the push carries" both read as covering this; it does not. Outside F-583's files (the hook is F-423's), so a new number, not a reopen.
Repro: In a scratch worktree of this repo (git worktree add --detach <path> HEAD): git switch -c zz-probe; commit one file whose content carries a fictional string; with PRIVATE_INSTANCE_PATTERNS set to that string, git push --dry-run origin zz-probe is refused by the hook ("pre-push: check-instance-data failed"). Then git switch --detach to a clean commit (the round's head) and run the same dry-run push: the hook prints "pre-push: instance-data gate on refs/heads/zz-probe (F-423: every ref)...", then "Instance-data check passed: 260 of 260 tracked files scanned, 2 private pattern(s) loaded ...", exits 0, and git reports "* [new branch] zz-probe -> zz-probe" (a real push would have published the planted commit). Measured 2026-10-24 on 77a21f9, dry run only; nothing was pushed, and the branch and worktree were removed.
Expected: the gate scans what the push carries: for each pushed local_sha (skipping deletions), the tree of that commit (or each commit in remote_sha..local_sha), e.g. the checker run against a temporary worktree or index of local_sha, the push refused if any fails. The line naming the ref then states the truth, and the Hooks: header line holds.
Fix: 2026-10-24 (builder) — on fix/instance-data-private-patterns-in-ci, commits 678a81c and 7b2e92d (PR #73; dev/hooks/pre-push and the bus header's Hooks: line; no plugin bytes) - Class, in one sentence: a gate that read the state it was standing in instead of the state being published. dev/hooks/pre-push now checks every commit the push adds to the remote (remote_sha..local_sha; for a new ref, everything not already on a remote ref) out into a temporary worktree, oldest first, and gates each there: the tip with its arm's full set (dev: the pushed tree's own doc-drift and stale-facts, then instance-data), every earlier commit with the instance-data gate, because a leak in an intermediate commit reaches the remote's history just the same. The instance-data gate is THIS checkout's checker (build/check-instance-data.mjs and build/lib.mjs copied over the temporary tree, where the script roots itself), so an older or weakened checker never judges its own push and a tree predating the gate is gated too. GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_PREFIX are cleared first; REQUIRE_PRIVATE_PATTERNS is set when the main checkout's config or the variable exists; deletions are skipped; every command inside the ref loop reads /dev/null so the ref list is never consumed; a trap removes the temporary worktree on every exit, Ctrl-C included; git's own reason is printed when the checkout fails; with ALLOW_MAIN_PUSH=1 main's tree is still instance-data gated. Measured here, dry runs only, nothing published: from the clean main checkout, a never-pushed branch whose tip was clean but whose first commit carried a planted string was refused on that commit ('check-instance-data failed on refs/heads/<probe> (pushed commit)'); a clean multi-commit ref passed; no temporary worktree or temp folder remained. The hook is installed by copy: after pulling, cp dev/hooks/pre-push .git/hooks/pre-push and cmp the two. Pick-up: re-install the hook, then the dry-run arms.
Judge: the tester's own dry-run pushes from a CLEAN checkout, nothing published: a branch with a planted tip, a branch whose planted string sits only in an intermediate commit under a clean tip, and a clean multi-commit ref - the first two refused naming the pushed commit, the third passed; every output searched for the planted string; afterwards git worktree list and the temp folder show nothing left behind.
Reopened: 2026-10-25 (tester, fix/instance-data-private-patterns-in-ci @ hb-20261024-02) — Acceptance round, first round of findings on this mechanism (born this release), so one round remains before the two-rounds valve. The kickoff's arms met their bars, PLANT (the kickoff's fictional string) absent from all hook output: H 'pre-push: gating the 1 pushed tree(s) of refs/heads/zz-r2-tip (F-423: every ref; F-584: the pushed trees, tip last)...' then 'pre-push: check-instance-data failed on refs/heads/zz-r2-tip (tip) (7bf15f0f7b88...)', exit 1; I 'gating the 2 pushed tree(s) of refs/heads/zz-r2-mid', refused 'on refs/heads/zz-r2-mid (pushed commit) (c2b2156d4a36...)'; J 'gating the 1 pushed tree(s) of refs/heads/zz-r2-clean', 'Instance-data check passed: 260 of 260 tracked files scanned, 2 private pattern(s) loaded (1 from gs-admin-explorer.config.json, 1 from PRIVATE_INSTANCE_PATTERNS', '* [new branch] HEAD -> zz-r2-clean', exit 0; K after every arm git worktree list held the main checkout and the tester's worktree only, and no gacd-prepush-* folder was in the temp folder; an interrupt mid-gate (SIGINT to the push's process group from a script, not a keyboard Ctrl-C) found gacd-prepush-mtfUGr at c2b2156 'locked' mid-gate and left neither it nor a .git/worktrees entry (the native git.exe then waited until stopped by hand, an artifact of the emulation); L read: line 72 copies this checkout's check-instance-data.mjs and lib.mjs over the pushed tree, the ALLOW_MAIN_PUSH=1 case falls through to the gate, every command in the ref loop reads /dev/null or inherits it from gate_tree. Also passed: a two-ref push (clean, then planted: refused on the second) and a tag ref (refs/tags/zz-r2-tag refused '(tip)'). The claim that fails: 'every commit the push adds to the remote (remote_sha..local_sha; for a new ref, everything not already on a remote ref)'. Class, in one sentence: the hook decides which commits are new to the remote from this repository's LOCAL tracking state - a tracking ref of ANY remote counts as published, and an old remote sha this repository lacks makes rev-list fail and the hook fall back to the tip alone - so when that local belief is foreign, stale or missing it gates fewer commits than the push publishes, fails open, and its 'gating the N pushed tree(s)' line understates N. Samples (dry runs from the clean main checkout, PRIVATE_INSTANCE_PATTERNS set to PLANT, zz-r2-mid = a commit carrying PLANT under a clean tip, which arm I refused): S3 a second remote's tracking ref (refs/remotes/zzfork/probe, what a fetch from a fork writes) at the planted commit - 'gating the 1 pushed tree(s) of refs/heads/zz-r2-mid', 'Instance-data check passed', '* [new branch] zz-r2-mid -> zz-r2-mid', exit 0; S3b a stale origin tracking ref (refs/remotes/origin/zz-r2-stale, a branch origin does not have: any clone that has not fetched since a remote history rewrite or branch deletion) - the same three lines, exit 0; deleting either ref brought back the refusal on c2b2156 '(pushed commit)'. S4 a forced push over a remote ref whose old sha this repository lacks (a local throwaway bare remote; the live shape is the PR page's Update branch merge or another clone's push, then a local --force) - 'fatal: Invalid revision range 9fbf7984...c0126892...', then 'gating the 1 pushed tree(s) of refs/heads/b', the pass line and '+ 9fbf798...c012689 zz-r2-mid -> b (forced update)', exit 0 (the fallback that sets commits to local_sha when the list is empty). On this machine today fetch.prune is true and git remote prune --dry-run origin lists nothing, and origin is the only remote: reachability is a second clone, a second remote, or a remote-side commit not yet fetched. Expected (the invariant, not a list): the gated set covers every commit reachable from local_sha that the RECEIVING remote does not have, judged against that remote (the hook's own arguments), never against other remotes or tracking refs that may be stale; when the hook cannot establish the set (rev-list fails, an old sha is missing) it refuses rather than gating the tip alone. Pass bar for the next round: S3, S3b and S4 each refused (on the planted commit, or as an undeterminable range), H to K re-run, and a sibling of the tester's choosing in the same class; PLANT absent from all output. Nothing published: git ls-remote --heads origin 'zz-*' printed nothing after every arm. Full shape: the tester's verdict comment on PR #73 @ hb-20261024-02.
Builder brief: 2026-10-25 (tester @ hb-20261024-02, at Bradley's direction: the two-rounds valve is a backstop, not the plan; the aim is to build and test this right the first time) — read before designing the fix. (1) The tester's error comes first. F-584's Expected line (round hb-20261024-01, tester) sketched a mechanism ('each commit in remote_sha..local_sha') instead of stating the requirement, and it said nothing about a new ref or an old sha this repository lacks. The fix filled that gap with an approximation, and this round reopened on the approximation. The requirement, stated once: every commit that the push makes reachable on the RECEIVING remote, and that the receiving remote does not already have, is gated; when the hook cannot establish that set, it refuses (fail closed) and says how to recover (fetch, then push again). (2) Realism, so the effort goes where it pays (this machine: one remote, fetch.prune true, one user). S4 is the real defect: on a force-push over a remote commit not yet fetched, the hook falls back to the tip and passes, and fail-open is the wrong default for a leak gate. S3 (a second remote's tracking ref counts as published) is unlikely today but cheap to close: count only the receiving remote, which is the hook's first argument. S3b (a stale tracking ref of the receiving remote) is close to theoretical here, and it may be met by a STATED LIMIT instead of code ('trusts this clone's fetched refs; fetch.prune is on') if closing it in code costs more than refusing an unresolvable range. (3) The design pattern behind the three reopens on F-583 and F-584: each Fix note claimed more than its code delivers ('every commit the push adds', 'nothing printed carries a private string'), so any input outside the approximation falsifies the claim. F-583's second fix broke the pattern by writing its limits down (four characters, the joined token), and this round's probe that hit a written limit (C5) went to the Noticed line, not to a reopen. Ask of this fix: write the claim at exactly the strength the code delivers, list its limits in the hook's comment block and in the Fix note, and fail closed wherever the hook cannot tell. (4) Judge before fix. The judge must be independent of the fixer's own cases, e.g. a differential that compares, for each probe state, the set of commits the hook gates with the set the receiving remote actually lacks. A local bare remote can stand in for origin, with the lacking set computed as git rev-list local_sha --not followed by every sha the bare remote's refs hold. Cover a new ref, an existing ref, a forced update with the old sha missing, a second remote, a stale tracking ref, a deletion and a multi-ref push. (5) The next round's bar, fixed now, before the fix: S3 and S4 refused (S4 may refuse as an undeterminable range); S3b refused, or covered by a stated limit; H to K re-run (K with a keyboard Ctrl-C); one sibling of the tester's choosing that tests the STATED claim within its stated limits. A case inside a stated limit goes to the Noticed line, never a reopen; only a break of the stated claim within its stated limits reopens. The tester states the round's bar from this line and does not invent a new one.
Fix: 2026-10-25 (builder) — (reopen 1) on fix/instance-data-private-patterns-in-ci, commit 03cfb73 (PR #73; dev/hooks/pre-push, build/test-pre-push-hook.mjs new and in the battery, AGENTS.md, docs-drift.yml, the bus Hooks: line; no plugin bytes) - Class, in one sentence: a gate that decided what the push publishes from this clone's belief about the remote (tracking refs of any remote, a range over an old sha it might lack) instead of asking the receiving remote. Now git ls-remote --heads --tags on the PUSH url (git's second argument to the hook) lists, once per push, what the remote holds; every commit reachable from a pushed tip and from none of those is gated oldest first in a temporary worktree, the tip in any case and last, each gated commit on its own stderr line; tracking refs play no part. Fail closed with the recovery named: the refs unreadable; a branch or tag tip this clone has not fetched (git fetch --tags, then push again); a ref that is not a commit; the checker cannot be staged. The claim is written at the strength the code delivers, with six stated limits in the hook's comment block: refs/pull/* count as new (more gating); an empty remote gates the whole history and a single-branch clone is refused until it fetches once; a shallow clone gates more; a change landing on the remote in the same moment is not seen (a deletion there can leave a commit counted as held); the judge is the pushing checkout's checker as its working tree stands; trees only - commit messages, identities, tag messages and ref names are F-588. Review of this fix round (/code-review medium as two cold finders on opus, 16 candidates): 13 fixed in 03cfb73 - the FETCH url was read where git hands the push url, so a pushurl apart from the fetch url was gated against the wrong repository (fail open); the checker was copied OVER the pushed tree's build/, so those two files' pushed versions were never scanned (fail open; staged beside the tree now); a locked worktree after an interrupted checkout survived a single --force; git's stderr merged into captured lists; replacement refs shaped the walk; HUP and QUIT untrapped under dash; the suite did not isolate global git config or the locale and one assertion was loose - 2 written as limits (the pushing checkout's checker; the same-moment race), 1 to F-588 (new, normal). ## F-589 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-25 (builder)
Severity: normal — code execution on a maintainer's machine from an unreviewed intermediate commit, reachable on any POSIX clone that installs the hook; not reachable on this machine, where it fails closed
Source: security review of PR #73 on 2026-10-25 (the finder's one candidate, filtered at 5 of 10 - below the review's reporting bar; logged on the owner's ruling for the next round touching dev/hooks/pre-push)
What: The pre-push hook stages this checkout's checker into a fixed path INSIDE the worktree holding the pushed tree (.gacd-prepush-gate/, with mkdir -p and cp), so on a clone that checks symlinks out as symlinks (core.symlinks true, the default on macOS and Linux) a pushed commit that tracks that path as a symlink into a folder of its own, with its own lib.mjs beside the target, has cp write through the symlink and node resolve the real path: the pushed tree's module runs with the maintainer's environment and can exit 0 to pass the gate, and the hook's claim that a weakened checker in the pushed tree never judges its own push does not hold there
Repro: On a core.symlinks=true clone with the hook installed: a branch whose one commit tracks .gacd-prepush-gate/check-instance-data.mjs as a symlink to ../sub/check-instance-data.mjs plus sub/check-instance-data.mjs and a sub/lib.mjs that prints a marker and exits 0; git push --dry-run origin that branch: the marker prints and the push passes. On this Windows machine (core.symlinks false) the symlink is a plain file, cp overwrites it and the push is refused - fails closed
Expected: the staging path cannot be pre-planted by the pushed tree: mkdir without -p (anything already at the path refuses the gate) or the checker staged in a separate mktemp -d outside the worktree with the tree root passed explicitly, node run with --preserve-symlinks-main; pinned by a probe in build/test-pre-push-hook.mjs that plants the symlink and expects the refusal, measured on the ubuntu runner where symlinks are real
Fix: 2026-10-25 (builder) — on fix/release-scope-root-fixes (PR #74 to dev; dev/hooks/pre-push, build/check-instance-data.mjs, build/test-pre-push-hook.mjs; no plugin bytes) - Class, in one sentence: a judge staged inside the thing it judges. The checker (check-instance-data.mjs and lib.mjs) is staged ONCE per push in its own mktemp -d OUTSIDE every worktree (gacd-prepush-gate-XXXXXX, removed by the same trap as the temporary worktree, Ctrl-C included) and pointed at each pushed tree with the checker's new --root, which roots git ls-files, the file reads and the config lookup (the tree's git-common-dir, so the main checkout's private config loads from a temporary worktree as before) at that tree; nothing in a pushed tree can pre-plant a folder the tree does not contain, and mkdir -p is gone with the staging folder. The Expected's --preserve-symlinks-main is not needed: the checker and its lib import each other from the staging folder, where no symlink of the tree's can sit. What: a fix round's wall clock is mostly its ceremony, not its fixes. Measured this round: the eleven fixes took about an hour to write; the judge arms and their suite runs about two hours (the dashboard suite is about 10 minutes per run as it drives every verb as a real process over the fixture tenant, and it ran four times, two of them on mistakes in the new arms); a predicted mutation sweep costs one full suite run per mutant (10 minutes each on the dashboard suite, so a four-mutant sweep is about 50 minutes); the cold-finder review about 20 minutes; the battery about 34 minutes and, by the F-573 rule, last — after the review's fixes — so it cannot overlap them. Each lever is written where its rule lives (AGENTS.md § Review-gate rules, the dev-loop skill's Step 2) when ruled, never improvised per round. Reported: 2026-10-14 (builder, R12 release-gate review, verifier traced)

What: the refresh lock is per dashboard, but re-documentation writes the KB-wide _manifest.json (manifest.mjs has no lock), so two dashboards of one KB refreshed at once can lose each other's documented / stale marks. The same property holds for every manifest writer.

Reopened: 2026-10-15 (builder, R13 polish round on claude/polish-pre-release-r13-6bdd49) — re-opened ahead of the release ceremony's step 0 on Bradley's word (the six once-deferred polish findings in one round). Fix: 2026-10-15 (builder) — (claude/polish-pre-release-r13-6bdd49, PR #60, hb-20261015-10) — Class, in one sentence: a file one script writes for every caller had no lock, so two callers at once lost each other's writes. manifest.mjs is the ONE writer of `_manifest.json` (the skills, describe-batch and the dashboard's re-documentation all spawn it), so the property lives there and every writer has it by construction: load() takes `_manifest.json.lock` beside the manifest through doc-lib's acquireFileLock (the exclusive-create primitive F-545 shares), save() releases it, and a verb that loads and never saves (report, a refusal) releases it at exit; a fresh holder makes the process wait, polling, up to `--lock-wait-seconds` (default 30; a number of seconds, 0 waits not at all) and then fail LOUDLY naming the holder's verb, pid and time and the lock file; a holder older than ten minutes is a dead writer's and is taken over, an unreadable lock file likewise. init writes a new manifest without loading and takes no lock (two inits of one KB are a setup fault). A second dashboard's refresh of the same KB therefore waits a few seconds at its re-documentation marks instead of racing. Pick up: /reload-plugins.
Judge: the real process against a held lock, not the primitive's own unit (test/manifest-ops.mjs "F-546"): a fresh lock held by another → mark waiting 0 s fails naming the holder with the manifest byte-equal and the holder's lock untouched; the lock released while a spawned mark waits → the mark lands after the release (timed, at least 400 ms in) and the lock is gone; a lock older than ten minutes, and an unreadable one → taken over, the mark lands; a non-number for --lock-wait-seconds refused; a read-only verb leaves no lock; no verb of the suite's 370-odd runs left one.

Reopened: 2026-10-16 (builder, release-gate review for 0.56.1; a verifier reproduced each on this Windows host with scratch drivers over the real doc-lib and manifest.mjs) — Class, in one sentence: acquireFileLock treats the lock file's record as the only evidence of a holder, and every way of failing to read one is resolved toward takeover or crash. Instances: (1) readHeld (doc-lib.mjs ~2818) turns a read or parse failure into {}, the age is NaN, and the stale test (~2838) unlinks and retakes a LIVE lock — the wx create (~2833) opens the file empty and writes it in a second call, and a reader in that gap sees "" (a quarter of reads in a two-process probe; a delete-pending EPERM read lands the same way); four processes × 300 acquisitions gave 5 takeovers of {} and ONE mutual-exclusion violation (two holders inside a wx-created critical section at once) — the lost mark this finding set out to stop. test/manifest-ops.mjs ~1836 writes "not json" and expects a takeover, so the suite bakes the window in. (2) In a stale takeover two takers both read the stale record: A unlinks and creates, B's later unlink removes A's fresh lock and B creates its own — both hold (traced; the comment at ~2843 assumes both unlinks precede both creates). (4) The lock is released in save() and on exit alone (manifest.mjs ~668), which SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGKILL all skip (measured), and nothing checks the holder is alive: an interrupt landing inside a mark (a Claude Code Esc, or the Bash tool's timeout killing describe-batch's tree) leaves _manifest.json.lock for ten minutes, during which every manifest verb — setup's and refresh's report and next, describe-batch (its first runManifest failure aborts the batch), the dashboard's re-documentation — waits 30 s and fails "locked by another writer" (a nine-minute-old dead lock still refused; an eleven-minute-old one taken). Expected: a record that cannot be read is held (fresh) until the FILE is older than staleMs; a holder whose pid is gone (process.kill(pid, 0) throwing ESRCH) is stale; the create and the unlinks go through the retry primitive; release re-reads and removes its own record only. Polish instances, same mechanism: load() (manifest.mjs ~622) takes the writer lock for the read-only verbs too (next, report, crawl without --set, reconcile-docs --dry-run) — on a KB directory the user cannot write, report now throws EPERM where it used to read, and a read can wait behind a writer (holds are milliseconds, so only as an amplifier of instance 4); the comment at ~646 names _manifest.lock while the file is _manifest.json.lock; no skill or template says what to do on the "locked" error, whose text invites removing the file by hand. A mechanism born in R13 (its first round): this is its second round of findings, so what the fix round leaves is deferred past 0.56.1 under the valve, never patched a third time.
Severity: normal — re-declared 2026-10-16 (builder): mutual exclusion is lost under contention and a killed writer locks the knowledge base for ten minutes; shipped behaviour wrong for a user, recoverable.
Fix: 2026-10-16 (builder, the release gate's fix round A on Bradley's ruling "fix the issues here — normal and polish") — (fix/r14-release-gate, PR #61, hb-20261016-02) — Class, in one sentence: the lock treated its record as the only evidence of a holder, and every failure to read one was resolved toward takeover or crash. doc-lib acquireFileLock redesigned: a holder is dead when its pid is gone from this machine (process.kill(pid, 0) throwing ESRCH; EPERM reads alive — measured on this host) or its record — or, while the record cannot be read, its FILE's mtime — is older than staleMs; an unreadable record on a young file is HELD (held.unreadable; the refusals say "its record is being written"); a dead file is CLAIMED by one rename to a dead-<pid> name (replaceFileSync; the loser's rename gets ENOENT and tries the create again), so two takers of one dead lock cannot both hold it; the wx create and every removal go through the Windows retry (replaceFileSync, removeFileSync); record() and release() re-read and act on this taker's own record alone. manifest.mjs: the read-only verbs (next, report, crawl without --set, reconcile-docs --dry-run) load with lock false — save() writes atomically, so a reader sees a whole file, never waits behind a writer, never fails on a folder it cannot write; the writers release on SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP as well as exit (on Windows a kill runs no handler, so the pid rule is the cure there); the "locked" text says a lock whose process is gone, or older than ten minutes, is taken over on its own; the comment names _manifest.json.lock. engagement.mjs writeSnapshotAndStore removes a stale store through removeFileSync. The skill's exit-1 line names the locked refusal and that it clears on its own; MAINTAINERS' manifest row names the lock. Tie-break, stated: root cause over the smallest change — the primitive rewritten and its stale suite rule rewritten with it, rather than the unreadable-is-dead rule patched; one new export (pidAlive). Valve: a mechanism born in R13 at its second round of findings — what the verdict round finds on it is deferred past the version being cut, never patched a third time.
Judge: the contention the reopen was measured with, never the fixer's list — the verifier's driver over the real doc-lib (four processes × 300 acquisitions holding 1 ms, then six × 200 holding none, each holder marking a wx-created critical section): 0 violations, 0 takeovers, 0 errors, every acquisition taken, where the same driver read one violation and five takeovers of {} on 0.56.1; test/doc-lib-fixtures.mjs's direct lock checks (an empty young file held; an old unreadable file taken over; a fresh record of a gone pid taken over at once; record and release leave another's lock; a live holder makes the taker wait) and its own 3 × 80 contention run with the marker; test/manifest-ops.mjs "F-546" rewritten to the new rules (the live holder is the suite's own process, the dead one a child that exited; an unreadable young file held, an old one taken over through utimes; report and next run with a live lock held, no wait, the lock untouched).
Mutation copy-out — sweep (source: each guard or branch this round's fixes added, reverted or weakened one at a time — the fixes' own arms, a vacuity check, not closure); predictions written to C:/m14/predictions.txt before the first run; each mutant on its own copy of the plugin (with the repo README and test/rig.mjs), then the suite that should see it:
    M1  an unreadable record counts as stale again (the reopen's rule; test/doc-lib-fixtures.mjs, test/manifest-ops.mjs)   KILLED pred:KILL
    M2  no pid liveness — a killed writer's fresh lock holds (doc-lib-fixtures, manifest-ops)                                   KILLED pred:KILL
    M3  the dead lock unlinked instead of claimed (two takers can both win; doc-lib-fixtures, manifest-ops)                    SURVIVED pred:SURVIVE
    M4  release() removes whatever lock is there (doc-lib-fixtures; F-545's property)                                           KILLED pred:KILL
    M5  the read-only verbs take the writer lock again (manifest-ops)                                                           KILLED pred:KILL
  (M3 survived as predicted: the two-taker takeover is a timing window no deterministic check closes — the claim is right by construction, a rename being atomic — and the contention runs cannot force the interleaving; a named gap, not closure.)
Sibling sweep: every taker of the primitive (grep acquireFileLock: manifest.mjs takeManifestLock, dashboard.mjs takeLock) reads the new rules through the one function; every unlinkSync left in a shipped script (grep: dashboard.mjs pruneSnapshots on the dashboard's own oldest snapshots — no handle holds one at prune time and a failure surfaces loudly; doc-lib's own removeFileSync body) read and left; the one process.on("exit") release (manifest.mjs) given its signal twins.
Verified: 2026-10-16 @ hb-20261016-02 (tester, R14 re-verification round; fix/r14-release-gate at b08c22d, clean and level, canary matched; a terminal in the workspace with --plugin-dir on the worktree; the SANDBOX KB, reads only, one one-program scratch dashboard (customer lists on, Health off, re-documentation on), removed after) — pass bar, stated before measuring (VALIDATION § R14 R1, the killed writer, and the Fix's claim that a holder whose pid is gone is dead): with a writer killed while `_manifest.json.lock` exists, `manifest.mjs report` exits 0 at once, and the next writer (a refresh's re-documentation) proceeds at once, the dead lock taken over — no 30 s wait, no "locked by another writer". HELD, with the precondition laid by hand, said: two live kills of a scratch refresh's process tree the moment the lock file appeared (a 2 ms poll, then a kill of the record's own pid) both landed after the holder, a `mark`, had released (its pid already gone: a mark takes milliseconds), so no dead lock was left live; `report` exited 0 in 0.07 s and 0.08 s (a read-only verb takes no lock now, so that half holds in any state). The dead writer's state was then laid down in the shape a killed mark leaves — a fresh record {"verb":"mark","pid":<a pid verified gone>,"at":<now>} created exclusively — and the next scratch refresh (re-documentation on, one stale template behind) re-documented through it: the template's doc and manifest entry written 5 s after the start, redocumented.templates.documented 1, nothing on stderr about a lock, no lock left. Suites at b08c22d: test/manifest-ops.mjs all pass ("F-546 a FRESH lock whose process is gone (a killed writer's) is a dead writer's: taken over at once (no wait) …", "… an unreadable lock file that is YOUNG is held …", "… the read-only verbs (report, next) run while a live writer holds the lock …" among them), test/doc-lib-fixtures.mjs 302 pass. Not re-run: the verifier's four-process contention driver (the Judge's own run); M3's two-taker claim stays by construction.

## F-548 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-15 (builder, R12 release gate — Bradley's question at F-529's ruling: with lists on, does a routine refresh update them?)
Severity: normal — with customer lists on, list membership is frozen at the last full pull: a routine (selective) refresh updates the kept accounts' figures but never who is on a list, so current membership costs a full pull every time (on the kept dashboard about 67 minutes against a selective refresh's 44)
What: Class, in one sentence: the cross-program lists are ranked only from data a full pull holds and the snapshot then folds away. A full pull reads every account's figures for every month, ranks, and keeps per-account rows only for the kept (listed, pinned) accounts; every other account's months become one "all other accounts" row per program and month. A selective refresh re-reads every account for the months it pulls (account units are planned per program per pulled month for all accounts), but the older months of the non-kept accounts are gone, so it cannot rank and carries the last full ranking (F-521, by design: rankedAt and carriedFrom say so). F-529's reselect is the same limit met at edit time.
Expected: the snapshot (or a sidecar beside the pages, never embedded in a page) keeps compact per-account totals by program and month for every account, so every refresh re-ranks exactly: stored months plus pulled months give the full pull's ranking (the judge: over unchanged data, a selective refresh's lists equal a full pull's, kind, n, floor, per, segment, kept, in order); a list change re-ranks from the store at no pull; the low-cadence quiet rule (per program) and per-segment lists (company fields for newly listed accounts) are kept. Contract: a 0.54.0 snapshot without the store is detected and the next refresh goes full, priced and said, with no hand step and no refusal. The store's size is measured on the kept dashboard's run directories before building, and the design stops if it is prohibitive.
Defer: 2026-10-15 (Bradley, R12 release gate) - past 0.54.0. Why not now: shipping 0.54.0 sooner is worth more than current membership on routine refreshes — a day-1 adopter's build is a full pull, most will not refresh for a month, the staleness is dated on the page and stated in the release notes, and the cost of waiting is one extra full refresh after session B. Reopen: session B, the fast follow after the 0.54.0 release (with F-530 and F-529's root).

From the store's cells alone plus the per-program cadence every pull reads for the whole window, selectAccountsAcross reproduced the full pull's three recorded lists IDENTICAL IN ORDER (25/25/25).

The store, as measured and ruled (Measured:, Ruling: above): engagement.mjs's reduce now hands back, beside the snapshot, an ACCOUNT STORE — its own account table for every company-linked account (and the no-link sends) by program and month over the window, both recipient classes, every send measure — written as plain JSON, one cell per line, at `snapshots/<stamp>.accounts.json` (accountStorePath, the ONE path rule the runner, export/import and the CLI's --out/--previous share), one per dashboard (the runner prunes the others). Every refresh ranks: a selective refresh takes its carried programs' carried months from the previous snapshot's store (carriedAccountCells) and its pulled months from the tenant, so the selection (selectionOver: the R24 picks per program and the cross-program lists, the least-engaged list joined by the low-cadence quiet accounts) and the account rows (accountRowsOf, ONE fold; carried rows keep their program-month's pull time) are a full pull's; per-segment lists rank on every refresh over the kept accounts with the fields the names call read for them (the newly listed ones included; a list over a field the pull did not read is notRanked "field-not-read", never every account under "(none)"). ## F-552 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-16 (builder, release-gate review for 0.56.1; verifier traced)
Severity: polish — a window of seconds; the pages regress until the next rebuild, nothing lost
What: rebuild and a display change (reselectFromStore and doConsequence, dashboard.mjs ~1986 and ~1755, reached from change and the interview's save) take no lock, while refresh holds the per-dashboard lock (takeLock, ~1815, its only caller); a rebuild or change that read snapshot X just before a refresh finishes writes the latest pages (and the publish) from X after the refresh wrote them from Y. A pruned snapshot recreated with no store does not happen: pruneSnapshots removes the oldest beyond KEEP_SNAPSHOTS only and X is the second-newest; pruneStores can remove X's store, after which rankChangedLists writes nothing.
Repro: start a refresh of a dashboard; in a second terminal run rebuild <slug> as the refresh ends; the pages show the previous pull.
Expected: rebuild and change take the refresh lock (or refuse while a refresh runs), so the pages always show the newest pull.
Fix: 2026-10-16 (builder, the release gate's fix round A) — (fix/r14-release-gate, PR #61, hb-20261016-02) — Class, in one sentence: a writer of the pages ran outside the lock that exists so the pages are written from one snapshot at a time. rebuild, and a change's rebuild or re-selection (doConsequence), run under the dashboard's lock (underLock → takeLock with the action's name): refused while a refresh runs — "a refresh of <slug> is already running: … — run rebuild again when it finishes" — and a change's refusal says the change IS saved and its rebuild did not run; a pull consequence is verbRefresh's own lock as before.
Judge: test/dashboard.mjs "F-552": a live lock held (the suite's own pid), rebuild refused naming it, a display change saved and its rebuild refused the same way, the lock untouched; the rebuild runs once the lock is gone and the page carries the saved change.
Mutation copy-out — sweep (source: the fix's own arm, a vacuity check, not closure; predictions in C:/m14/predictions.txt before the run; one copy of the plugin per mutant):
    M8  rebuild and change take no lock (test/dashboard.mjs "F-552")                                                            KILLED pred:KILL
Sibling sweep: every writer of latest-*.html (grep buildPages callers: rebuildFrom alone, reached from verbRefresh under its lock, verbRebuild and doConsequence under underLock) — one builder, every caller locked.
Verified: 2026-10-16 @ hb-20261016-02 (tester, R14 re-verification round; fix/r14-release-gate at b08c22d, clean and level, canary matched; a terminal in the workspace with --plugin-dir on the worktree; the SANDBOX KB, reads only, one one-program scratch dashboard (customer lists on, Health off, re-documentation on), removed after) — pass bar, stated before measuring (VALIDATION § R14 R2): `rebuild <scratch>` from a second process during a refresh exits 1 with "already running … run rebuild again when it finishes", the pages untouched; after the refresh the same line exits 0. HELD both ways, on the scratch's second refresh: rebuild 1.8 s in, exit 1, error "a refresh of "<scratch>" is already running: started by <user> at 2026-10-16T20:17:30.338Z (0 minutes ago, pid 16504) — run rebuild again when it finishes; …", both latest pages byte-equal (md5) and the lock untouched; after the refresh (exit 0, its lock released) the same line exit 0, the pages rebuilt. Said: during the scratch's FIRST refresh the same line was refused "no snapshot of "<scratch>" yet — run `… refresh <scratch> --kb <kb>` first" (exit 1): the no-snapshot check runs before the lock, so the arm needs a snapshot. The change's half (a display change saved, its rebuild refused) is the suite's: test/dashboard.mjs "F-552 …" PASS.

Reported: 2026-09-29 (builder, consumer follow-up (b) of dev-utils F-026, which shipped the `Dev-only:` bus header line in dev-utils 0.5.0)

Fix: 2026-09-29 (builder) — Class confirmed: consumer-parity — one fact, the release strip set, held by eight readers that each kept their own copy. The declaration is now the bus header's `Dev-only: dev plugins/gs-superadmin/skills/dev-canary`, written by `dev-utils init --dev-only` (0e5a0b1; `dev-utils status` lists both paths with no `!!`), read together with the `Canary:` line because dev-utils strips the canary with the declared paths. build/dev-only.mjs is the one reader and a CLI (`node build/dev-only.mjs` prints the set). Its grammar is dev-utils' check_dev_only; it is stricter only toward refusing (a missing line, or a second one, is refused: the checks anchor on the line). Every reader moved onto it: check-doc-drift checks 1-3 (the skill filter), 4 (the canary's name, from Canary:, and its allowance), 17, and 18 (needles derived per path, repo-relative and plugin-relative; a one-segment path needs a child and never heads an absolute path, so /dev/null stays green and ../dev/X does not). New check 24 holds both workflow steps to the reader: each must run it and spell no strip path itself. Prose points at the line: CLAUDE.md (repo map, release bullet), CONTRIBUTING.md, and RELEASE-CHECKLIST §3, whose strip is `git rm … $(node build/dev-only.mjs)` plus two verify commands (one commit beyond dev; no declared path survives). §5 is `dev-utils release-finish`. The cut stays by hand: Bradley's decision 2026-09-29 over `dev-utils release`, because nothing is pushed until the stripped tree is green, and a red leg after the push is recut onto the same branch, so the PR stays open. Where a tree the strip already ran on gets the set (kickoff item 2): the working-tree bus when there is one; else HEAD's (the rehearsal arm strips the worktree and index and commits nothing); else origin/dev's (a release branch, the release PR, main — release-finish's own answer); none is refused, never read as an empty set. docs-drift.yml fetches dev shallowly (`git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin +refs/heads/dev:refs/remotes/origin/dev`) only when the tree has no bus. Judged not "is this dev-only?" questions, so left alone: check-stale-facts' FLAG_EXCLUDE and CITATION_EXCLUDE, and check-doc-drift's check 13 dev/ exclusion, LC_EXCLUDE and BOM_EXCLUDE. Each keys on dev/ as the loop's record (a frozen archive, bus prose quoting old spellings), which would hold even if dev/ shipped. Found by the rehearsal before handoff: the suite's first run on a stripped shape crashed (a refusal case left a malformed bus in the rig's HEAD and the stripped-only arm read it); fixed in the suite, and re-run on all three shapes. The mutation sweep below left one unpinned arm (M10), now pinned by a control case. Reload: nothing to reload — no plugin byte changed (build, CI and docs only; no version bump).

Verdict: REOPENED 2026-09-29 (tester, F-469 acceptance round) @ hb-20260929-01. Under test: branch fix-f469-dev-only (PR #35, unmerged), checkout clean and level with origin at 8b8596c (the handoff commit); the dev-canary skill's description read hb-20260929-01 in session. Round type: ACCEPTANCE — the first verdict on a new mechanism (the Dev-only: line as the one declaration, read by build/dev-only.mjs). Every measurement ran in a scratch clone of the branch; the repo's working tree was not edited until this verdict.
Pass bar (stated before measuring, from the Fix note): (a) change the Dev-only line (add a path, drop one) and every reader follows with no second edit — check-doc-drift checks 1-4, 17, 18 and 24, `node build/dev-only.mjs`, and docs-drift.yml's two strip-set step bodies; (b) a tree the strip already ran on gets the set from HEAD (rehearsal shape) or origin/dev (release shape), and a missing or malformed declaration is refused loudly, never read as an empty set; (c) the reader's grammar agrees with dev-utils' check_dev_only (the reader's documented extra strictness — no line, or a second line — excepted).
Measured (a): 25 Dev-only values through the reader, `dev-utils status` and check-doc-drift. Dropping the canary dir from the line still strips it (Canary: joins); `none`, `NONE` and a dropped `dev` turn dev/ into shipped docs and check 4 reds on the archive's canary mentions (it follows); adding a shipped skill dir (skills/audit) is stripped by both workflow bodies and the stripped tree reds on the README's /gs-superadmin:audit references (it follows). What fails: adding a FILE at the plugin root — `plugins/gs-superadmin/MAINTAINERS.md` — leaves check-doc-drift exit 0 ("112 shipped files name none of it"), while 7 mentions in 5 shipped files (README, CHANGELOG, describe-batch.mjs x2, doc-lib.mjs, setup's document-domain-notes.md) are the dangling pointers check 18 exists to catch. Check 18 derives a plugin-relative spelling per path, and that spelling is ONE segment (`MAINTAINERS.md`), so the rule built for the repo-root word `dev` — a one-segment spelling needs a child after it — applies and no mention of a file can ever have one. The repo-relative spelling is still derived, but shipped text addresses plugin files plugin-relatively.
Class (the invariant, not an instance list): for every declared strip path P, a shipped-file mention of P in the spelling shipped text actually uses for it (plugin-relative when P lies inside the plugin, repo-relative otherwise) reds check 18. The child requirement is a property of a one-segment spelling that is also an English word, not of every one-segment spelling. Falsifiable test that enumerates nothing: for each path P on a mutated line and each tracked file F under P, append a Markdown link to F's plugin-relative path to a shipped .md; check 18 must red naming P. Measured violated for P = a plugin-root file; the same test holds for every multi-segment P tried and for dev/.
Measured (b): all green. Rehearsal shape (mutated line committed, adding skills/audit): the strip body, run verbatim under bash -eo pipefail, removed the three paths; the reader then named HEAD:dev/FEEDBACK.md; the existence body exited 0, and 1 naming skills/audit once that dir alone was restored. Release shape (origin = the clone itself, dev = a branch carrying the mutated line, a throwaway release/* branch): RELEASE-CHECKLIST §3's strip and commit ran verbatim; its verify printed 1 and nothing; the fetch and existence bodies read origin/dev:dev/FEEDBACK.md and exited 0. Refusals: a malformed line (`dev ../x`) in the worktree bus, in HEAD's and an origin/dev bus with no line each exit 1 through the step bodies; no bus anywhere is refused naming `git fetch origin dev`; §3's strip with a refused reader dies at git rm (No pathspec, 128).
Measured (c): the 25 values agree refused-vs-accepted with `dev-utils status`, apart from the documented second line (a column-0 Dev-only: inside a header comment block: the reader refuses, dev-utils reads the first). Tab, NBSP, U+001C, a trailing backslash, ./dev, dev/, CRLF and a missing space after the colon split and normalize alike; U+FEFF is refused by both as untracked. One framing divergence the value-level differential cannot see: dev-utils reads the bus with universal newlines, so a lone CR is a line break there and not in the reader. `Dev-only: dev<CR>plugins/gs-superadmin/skills/email-report` makes the reader strip email-report while dev-utils strips dev alone, and `Load-x: y<CR>Dev-only: dev` is refused by the reader while dev-utils reads it. Recorded as evidence, not as a reopen: no editor or dev-utils verb writes a lone CR.
Not reopened by: checks 1-4, 17 and 24, the reader's grammar and its three bus sources, the workflow bodies, §3's strip. Noted, not reopening (pre-existing, same as dev's SHIPPED_STRIP_REF): check 18 does not see a backslash spelling (dev\VALIDATION.md) or a bare dir mention (the dev/ folder). §3's second verify loop prints the refusal on stderr but exits 0 when the reader refuses, so its "prints nothing" pass signal is carried only by what the operator reads.

## F-470 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-03 (tester, S1-V on feat/jo-dash-s1-facts @ hb-20261003-01; production tenant, reads only; found while choosing V9's P-unsub program, before any run of the adapter)
Severity: normal — on a tenant whose unsubscribe link carries none of the classifier's wording, the adapter counts unsubscribe clicks as content clicks: the click rate R18 defines is overstated, and a template can read `tracked` on unsubscribe clicks alone
What: `classifyLink` (plugins/gs-superadmin/scripts/engagement.mjs, `NON_CONTENT_LINK_RULES`) calls a clicked link content unless it is `mailto:` or matches `unsubscribe | opt-out | email-preferences | manage-preferences`. On the measured tenant the emails' unsubscribe link is not a Gainsight URL: it is a preferences-center page on the company's own website, and its path words it as `<word>-preferences-center` (once as `<word>-<word>-preferences-email`). The pattern matches neither, so every such click classifies as content. Over the 13-month window ~10^1 clicked sends carried that link, one program's only clicked send among them; in a 5000-row sample of the year before the window it was the most-clicked link of all (~10^3 sends). No clicked URL in either read classified as unsubscribe or mailto.
Repro: one catalog-checked read of `email_log_v2` plain rows (`SourceId`, `EmailTemplateId`, `ExecutedDate`, `LinkClickedJson`) with `Source EQ "Advanced Outreach"`, `AddressType EQ "To"`, a two-sided `ExecutedDate` window, `LinkClickedCount GT 0` and `--page-size 5000`. Unwrap each row's entries, reduce every URL to host plus path skeleton (ids masked, query values dropped) and classify each with `classifyLink`: every skeleton reads content, the site's preferences-center page included.
Expected: Bradley's ruling (2026-10-03): the unsubscribe link is a per-tenant input. Set-up asks whether an external domain or link is used for unsubscribes, and the classifier treats a match as not content, beside its generic patterns. Tenant specifics are spec parameters, never hardcoded (the plan's house rule 13); where the question is asked (workspace setup or the dashboard interview), the spec field and the adapter input are the builder's to settle with Bradley. It rides the S1 builder batch with the V0 changes; V9 at the S1-V re-run verifies it on the chosen P-unsub, its run lines passing the new input.
Fix: 2026-10-03 (builder, S1 fix batch on feat/jo-dash-s1-facts, PR #36 unmerged) — Class, in one sentence: a fact about ONE tenant (which page its recipients unsubscribe on) was carried by a wording pattern applied to EVERY tenant, so the pattern is right only where the tenant happens to use its words. The fix is the input Bradley ruled, not a wider pattern. Three decisions he took at this batch's kickoff: (1) the input is a link or a host and it repeats; (2) the generic patterns do NOT widen (a wider built-in pattern runs unchecked on every tenant and would drop real content clicks); (3) the dashboard interview asks for it, beside internal domains. What changed in scripts/engagement.mjs: a new flag, `--unsubscribe-link <link|host>`, repeatable. A value with a path names that host (or a subdomain of it) and that path or anything under it, by whole path segments; scheme, query, letter case and a trailing slash are ignored. A value with no path names the whole host. It is parsed as a URL, never matched as a substring, and a value that names no web host is refused at the command line. `classifyLink` treats a match as not content, after `NON_CONTENT_LINK_RULES`, which are unchanged and still decide first. It is a run parameter: echoed in `meta.params.unsubscribeLinks` (normalized, sorted; empty when none is given); part of the run's identity, so a run directory resumes only with the input it started with; and a change to it, in either direction, forces a full refresh in `decideRefresh` ("the unsubscribe links changed"), as a change of internal domains does. One thing the report did not list and the class reaches: click EVIDENCE. Reduce merged each template's click history from the previous snapshot on every refresh, full ones included, so a template the old input called tracked on unsubscribe clicks would have stayed tracked after the input was set. History now carries only from a snapshot classified under the same input. Added for the tester: `honesty.clicks.byUnsubscribeInput`, the clicked sends with at least one link the input named; 0 means the input matched nothing. Sibling built, not in the report: another page of the same site whose path only BEGINS like the named page (the fixture's look-alike) must stay content, and does; so does the site's home page, and the same path on another host. Where the fact lives: nowhere in the repo; it is the tenant's, so no table gained a row. Other tenant-shaped constants in the adapter were read for the same class and left: the JO source name and the two response-status labels are product values the spike matched against the UI, and internal domains were already an input. What the tester does: this is verified by V9 of the S1-V re-run (dev/VALIDATION.md § ENG-2, rewritten for it): pass the tenant's unsubscribe link on every run line; P-unsub must read zero content clicks, its templates `unknown`, `nonContentOnly` above zero and `byUnsubscribeInput` above zero. Reload: /reload-plugins (a script changed; no hook, no skill).
Judge: offline, the engagement suite's oracle: the fixture generator records which of each send's clicked links are content when it writes them, and the snapshot's clicked counts must equal a straight count of that record, with no classifier and no reducer in the count. With the input passed they are equal on the own-site fixture; without it they are not, which is the defect reproduced. The judge of record is the tester's live arm, V9, on the tenant's real links: the fixture's link is one this session wrote, so it cannot show that the real link's shape is covered.
Mutation copy-out — sweep (source: the decision points of this batch's three changes in scripts/engagement.mjs — the F-470 input, and the two contract changes riding with it; a vacuity check on the committed checks, not closure); predictions written before the run; suites = test/engagement.mjs + test/contract-conformance.mjs:

    M2   roll-up: not-tracked when ANY template is  KILLED pred:KILL

    M4   resp-total: the Responded filter dropped  SURVIVED pred:SURVIVE
    M5   the all-time response call is never planned  KILLED pred:KILL
    M6   all-time Partially submitted counted as Submitted  KILLED pred:KILL
    M7   readResponses(months) hands back the all-time denominator  KILLED pred:KILL
    M8   readResponses() all-time counts read from responseParticipants swapped  KILLED pred:KILL
    M9   classifyLink ignores the tenant's links  KILLED pred:KILL
    M10  matcher: the path segment boundary dropped  KILLED pred:KILL
    M11  matcher: subdomain test without its dot  KILLED pred:KILL
    M12  matcher: path compared case-sensitively  KILLED pred:KILL
    M13  decideRefresh: a changed input no longer forces a full refresh  KILLED pred:KILL
    M14  reduce: click history carried whatever the input  KILLED pred:KILL
    M15  fetch: click payloads classified without the run's links  KILLED pred:KILL
    M16  meta.params no longer echoes the input  KILLED pred:KILL
    M17  resolveParams: values not sorted  KILLED pred:KILL
    M18  parseUnsubscribeLink: a word with no dot accepted as a host  KILLED pred:KILL
    M19  parseUnsubscribeLink: a link with a user part accepted  KILLED pred:KILL
    M20  byInput never counted  KILLED pred:KILL
    M21  the tenant's links decide before the generic rules  KILLED pred:KILL
    M22  run identity: the input left out of the resume comparison  KILLED pred:KILL
    M23  resolveParams: duplicate values kept  KILLED pred:KILL
    M24  reduce: all-time counts kept for programs outside the selection (guard dropped) SURVIVED pred:SURVIVE
  24 of 24 as predicted. The three predicted survivors are equivalent on any reachable state, not unpinned arms: M3 (a selected program always has at least one send, so it always counts a template), M4 (a row with a Submitted or Partially Submitted status is a responded row; the filter mirrors the monthly call's), M24 (the row list is built from the denominator's programs, which are already limited to the selection).
Pass bar (stated before measuring, from VALIDATION section ENG-2's V9 and this Fix note): with both unsubscribe links passed on every run line, `meta.params.unsubscribeLinks` echoes them; P-unsub reads `clicked` 0 on every one of its rows and its templates read `unknown`; `honesty.clicks.nonContentOnly` > 0 and `honesty.clicks.byUnsubscribeInput` > 0.
Not verified: 2026-10-03 (tester, S1-V re-run @ hb-20261003-02, feat/jo-dash-s1-facts clean at 9482657, production tenant, reads only) — the bar could not be measured, so the status stays FIXED: every quantity in it reads the snapshot, and run 2 built none (F-471 and F-472 left it partial; runs 3-5 were not run, on Bradley's call). The input passed was the tenant's two unsubscribe pages, both on the company's own site, as the emails print them (host with www, page path, trailing slash). Diagnostic, not the bar: run 2's click-json payload, which the fetch classifies under the run's input, holds 1591 clicked sends; 59 carry at least one link the input named, and 36 have only non-content links, every one of them an input match. So for those 59 sends, blind spot (1) of this handoff (a stored tracking redirect that would not match) did not occur: the log stored the page links themselves, and the host-and-path matcher caught them in the form the emails print; a wrapped link elsewhere would read as content and is not excluded by this count. P-unsub's rows and template states need the click attribution that F-471 blocks. V9 carries to the next re-run with the same inputs.
Verified: 2026-10-03 (tester, S1-V second re-run @ hb-20261003-03, feat/jo-dash-s1-facts clean and level with origin at 96ed11e, the dev-canary skill read hb-20261003-03 in session; production tenant, reads only) — RE-VERIFICATION round: the verdict against the pass bar above, stated before measuring, and nothing past it. Same inputs as the first re-run on every run line (both unsubscribe pages as the emails print them). Measured on run 2's snapshot (full refresh, completed): `meta.params.unsubscribeLinks` echoes both, normalized to host/path and sorted; P-unsub has 6 rows, `clicked` 0 on every one, and its 3 templates read `unknown` (program roll-up `unknown`, templates {tracked 0, notTracked 0, unknown 3}); `honesty.clicks.nonContentOnly` 36 and `honesty.clicks.byUnsubscribeInput` 59. Runs 3, 4 and 5 read the same echo and both counts above zero. Pass. Beside the bar, logged on its own: F-473 (clicked sends with no company link never reach attribution), a different mechanism from this input.

## F-471 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-03 (tester, S1-V re-run on feat/jo-dash-s1-facts @ hb-20261003-02; production tenant, reads only; VALIDATION section ENG-2, V8, run 2)
Severity: normal — the adapter cannot finish any run through the real CLI: its click-attribution call is refused before it is sent, so the run ends partial and reduce builds no snapshot. No skill calls the script yet and PR #36 is unmerged, so no user reaches it; V8's failure already holds the merge.
What: the `click-attr` family (plugins/gs-superadmin/scripts/engagement.mjs, `FAMILIES`) groups by `Gsid` (with program, template, month and the company path) and shows only `countOf`, which is COUNT of `Gsid`. CLI 1.0.10 normalizes every `rp run` request before sending it (its dist/artifacts/validators/report.js, `normalizeGroupByDedup`): it drops each show field whose key equals a group-by field's key, and the key is `objectName::fieldName`, with the aggregation ignored. So COUNT of email_log_v2.Gsid reads as a duplicate of the grouped email_log_v2.Gsid and is dropped; the show list is then empty, and `assertShowFieldsNonEmpty` refuses the request client-side. The adapter classifies that failure `other`, correctly neither retried nor split, so all three click-attr units (all, and one per internal domain) fail on every run, on any tenant, whatever its click volume: the call is always planned. The stand-in CLI (test/fixtures/engagement/acme-tenant.mjs) does not model the normalizer, so the suites stay green. The spike recorded the rule's warning text (SPIKE-NOTES' error list: exit 0, with another show field left); the refusal case was never exercised.
Repro: from a consumer workspace with the plugin loaded from this branch, `node .gs-superadmin/plugin/scripts/engagement.mjs run --kb <slug> --internal-domain '<domain>' --run <id> --out <file>` exits 4 with status partial, and its fetch-log.jsonl records each click-attr unit `failed`, kind `other`, with this stderr (as the log records it):
    [report] normalizeGroupByDedup: removed 1 showField(s) already present in groupByFields. Error: Report must have at least one entry in showFields (spec 2.1, EMPTY_SHOW_ME_FIELDS).
Expected: the clicked-sends attribution reaches the server, and a run with no other failure completes. The class, as an invariant rather than a list: no family's built query shows a field whose objectName::fieldName, keyed as the CLI keys it, equals one of its group-by fields', because the CLI deletes such a show field silently when another remains and refuses the call when none does. A falsifiable test that enumerates nothing: put the CLI's own normalization in front of the stand-in CLI, or run every family's built query through `normalizeGroupByDedup` and `assertShowFieldsNonEmpty` keyed exactly as the CLI keys, and require every family in `FAMILIES`, default and step detail, to pass through unchanged. Unmeasured live, because run 3 did not run: `step-click` groups by a lookup path whose leaf is `Gsid` and shows COUNT of `Gsid` on ao_emails; whether the CLI keys that path with the log's object or the hop target decides whether it collides, and the test above settles it offline. The CLI's aggregation-blind comparison is arguably an upstream quirk, worth a /gs-superadmin:report-bug report, but the adapter is pinned to 1.0.10 and has to work with it.
Fix: 2026-10-03 (builder, second S1 fix batch on feat/jo-dash-s1-facts, PR #36 unmerged) — Class, in one sentence: the adapter asked for a request shape the CLI rewrites before sending, and the stand-in CLI answered the request as written, so the suites certified a query the real CLI never sends. Three changes. (1) The query: `click-attr` still groups by the send's id, and now counts a field it does not group by (COUNT of LinkClickedCount, which its own filter guarantees is set); its reader never read the count, only the group columns, so nothing downstream moved. (2) The invariant, by construction: `validateQuery`, which every `rp run` already passes through before it is spawned, now refuses any query that shows a field it also groups by, keyed as the CLI keys (object and field name; a lookup path by the object its last hop lands on and its leaf; aggregation and date bucket ignored). A future family with the collision fails offline, naming the field, instead of at a tenant. (3) The stand-in CLI now applies the CLI's rule before answering: it drops the colliding show field with the CLI's warning, and refuses with the CLI's error text when none is left. That is your first falsifiable test, and it is what makes the suites able to see this class. Your open question, settled offline: `step-click` does NOT collide. The handler keys a lookup path by the hop target, so its group is email_log_v2::Gsid and its count is ao_emails::Gsid. Not done here, and yours or Bradley's to decide: the upstream report (/gs-superadmin:report-bug) on the aggregation-blind comparison. What the tester does: /reload-plugins, then the re-run from run 1 on the new token; V8 judges this (every family ends ok, click-attr included, with no dropped-show-field warning on any call).
Judge: the installed CLI's own code, not this session's model of it: a scratch script imported `normalizeGroupByDedup` and `assertShowFieldsNonEmpty` from the pinned CLI's dist/artifacts/validators/report.js (1.0.10, read from disk; no tenant call) and ran every family's built query through them, all 16 families in every recipient class they are built for. Every one came back unchanged, and the click-attr shape as handed off at hb-20261003-02 was refused with the message you recorded, so the judge reproduces the defect before it passes the fix. Its one hand-derived input is how a field spec becomes the object and field name the CLI keys on; that was read from the handler (the aggregation and the date bucket keep the field's own key, a lookup path takes the last hop's object). The judge of record is V8 on the tenant.

## F-472 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-03 (tester, S1-V re-run on feat/jo-dash-s1-facts @ hb-20261003-02; production tenant, reads only; VALIDATION section ENG-2, V8, run 2)
Severity: normal — on a tenant with a mass-send day, every full run ends partial, so it builds no snapshot. No user reaches it today (unmerged; no skill calls the script), and V8's failure already holds the merge.
What: the `account` family's split ladder is programs, then day, then the IsOpened and IsSent flags, and `runUnit` fails a unit with "nothing left to split on" when the last rung still returns a full page. At account grain the row count grows with the distinct accounts a program reaches inside one partition, not with time, so a program-day reaching more than 5000 accounts in one opened/sent partition can never fit, whatever the ladder does. Measured: of 167 account calls, 32 returned a full 5000-row page; 27 of them split further and completed, and 5 units, each one program on one day in one opened/sent partition, still returned exactly 5000 rows. They cover three programs (one program-day in three of its four partitions, two others in one each; two of the three days are the last day of one month and the first of the next). These are the tenant's mass-send days: one Email Chain sent ~3 x 10^5 emails in a single month, observed at the first S1-V round. The fictional tenant has no program-day that large, so the suites cannot see it. The truncated payloads stay on disk but are unusable: the unit is failed, and reduce refuses a partial run.
Repro: the run line in F-471 on a tenant with such a day. The run's summary lists each unit under `failed` with kind `truncated` and "nothing left to split on"; fetch-log.jsonl shows each one with one program id, a one-day window, two flag partitions and 5000 rows.
Expected: the class, as an invariant: a family whose grain carries an entity key (account, send, participant) can cut a unit by that key, or by some other dimension that bounds the rows per call, below one program-day; time and flags bound the rows only for families whose grain is time-shaped. A falsifiable test: a fixture program-day whose distinct accounts exceed the page in every flag partition completes, with totals equal to the oracle's. Siblings with the same floor, not tripped on this tenant: `click-attr` and `click-json` (a row per clicked send; ladder programs, then day) and `step-click` (a row per clicked send). The measured tenant's 1591 clicked sends over 13 months fit in one click-json call, so the click families are far from it today.
Fix: 2026-10-03 (builder, second S1 fix batch on feat/jo-dash-s1-facts, PR #36 unmerged) — Class, as you stated it: a split ladder whose rungs bound the rows only for time-shaped grains, under a family whose rows grow with an entity count. The fix adds one last rung, taken from your "some other dimension that bounds the rows per call": the unit is cut by the RECIPIENT'S ADDRESS. A unit still full at one program, one day and one flag partition splits into the sends whose address contains a character and the sends whose address does not, then again on the next character, down a fixed list of 36 (letters and digits; no punctuation, which a server could read as a pattern wildcard). Why this dimension: the measures are additive, so any cut of the SENDS that puts each send in exactly one half adds up to the same account rows (an account with recipients in both halves gets a row in each, and reduce sums them); CONTAINS and DOES_NOT_CONTAINS on the same character are each other's complement; and both operators are ones the spike measured on this exact field, which the internal and external class filters already rely on. A cut by the account key itself would need an operator on the lookup field that nothing has measured. Only a single character ever reaches a filter; no address does. The rung is on every family with your floor: account, click-attr, click-json, template, and step and step-click on the JO log's own address field. Distinct counts (the uniques and participant families) are never cut by it: they do not add up across a cut. The ladder still ends: when the characters run out the unit fails as before, and the run is partial. Cost: each extra level re-asks a full page, so a mass-send day adds a few calls per level; your run 2 would have added calls only under the 5 failed units. What the tester does: /reload-plugins, then the re-run from run 1 on the new token. Start a NEW --run name rather than resuming run 2's directory: a resume would work (the kept truncated units now split further), but it would reduce calls pulled hours apart, and opens arriving in between can make the template and account tables disagree for a reason that is not a defect. V8 judges this (no `truncated` unit in `failed`), and V1's reconciliation judges the cut itself.
Judge: offline, your falsifiable test, built as a fixture: a program that sends to sixty accounts on one day, pulled at a 20-row page, so one opened-and-sent partition of that day holds more accounts than the page. The run completes, and the suite's oracle (a straight count of the fixture's rows, no query and no reducer) must equal the template table and the account table's totals. What decides it on a real tenant, independently of this session, is the adapter's own reconciliation: `accounts-sum-to-program` compares the account table with the template table per program, month and measure, and the template table with the cheap tenant-wide count. If the two operators are not exact complements on real addresses (a null address, a case rule), a send is lost or counted twice and that check goes red, naming the program and month. So V1 on the re-run is the judge of record, with V8.
Sibling sweep: the split ladders of all 16 families were read for the same floor. Given the rung: account, template, click-attr, click-json, step, step-click (every family whose rows are sends or grow with an entity count and whose measures add up). Not given it, with the reason: uniques-month, uniques-window, participants-month, participants-window (distinct counts); sent-since and classes (a handful of rows per program or per source); resp-month, resp-participants and resp-total (survey_participant carries no address; rows are programs times statuses); account-names (cut by its key list already).
Mutation copy-out — sweep (source: the decision points of this fix in scripts/engagement.mjs; a vacuity check on the committed checks, not closure); predictions written before the run; suites = test/engagement.mjs + test/contract-conformance.mjs:
    N4   account: no address rung  KILLED pred:KILL
    N5   address rung: both halves CONTAINS (no complement)  KILLED pred:KILL
    N6   address rung: the character is picked by the whole partition's length  KILLED pred:KILL
    N7   the JO send log cut on the delivery log's address field  KILLED pred:KILL
    N8   click-json: no address rung  KILLED pred:KILL
    N9   account: the address rung tried before the flags  SURVIVED pred:SURVIVE
    N10  the cut list shortened to one character  KILLED pred:KILL
  7 of 7 as predicted. N9, the predicted survivor, is a cost choice, not a correctness one: either order of the last two rungs yields the same totals.
Known limit: 2026-10-03 (builder, from an independent read of this fix before handoff) — the cut covers every send only if a send with NO address at all lands in the does-not-contain half. The stand-in CLI puts it there; nothing measured says the real server does, and if it does not, that send is in neither half. For the template and account families the reconciliation checks would go red. For the click families nothing would: a clicked send with no address would simply not be counted. The same assumption already sits under the external-recipient filter, which the first build shipped. It is not patched here, because the exact fix needs an is-null filter shape nothing has measured either, and a wrong one would fail the very runs this fix exists to complete. Instead the precondition is banked as one read in dev/VALIDATION.md section ENG-2: the count of in-scope sends whose address is null. Zero makes the limit moot on that tenant; above zero, reopen this section with the count.
Pass bar (stated before measuring, from VALIDATION section ENG-2 as re-banked at hb-20261003-03): V8, no unit in `failed` is `truncated`; V1, a unit cut by the recipient's address still adds up (the account and template tables agree on every measure of every program and month the cut touched); and the banked read for the known limit, the count of in-scope sends with a null address: zero, nothing more; above zero, reopen.

V8: `failed: []` in all four runs; run 2's account family made 265 calls, 76 of them full pages that split further, and none was left truncated (run 3: the same, plus `step` 25 of 25 ok on the JO log's own address field). V1: the adapter's `accounts-sum-to-program` is red, so the cut was judged on its own, against a count that does not go through the adapter: in all 561 program-months of run 2, template-table sent minus account-table sent equals that program-month's count of sends with no company link, from one direct grouped read (561 of 561 equal, 0 differ), the mass-send month the cut split deepest included. Every other measure's mismatch sits in those same program-months, apart from two in the current month on one mass-send program where sent agrees and delivered (6) and opened (1) differ: status changing between calls minutes apart (F-475), not the cut, which would move sent. So the red is F-473 (a send with no company link leaves the account table entirely), a different mechanism, logged on its own; the cut adds every send exactly once.
