## F-473 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-03 (tester, S1-V second re-run on feat/jo-dash-s1-facts @ hb-20261003-03; production tenant, reads only; VALIDATION section ENG-2, V1, run 2)
Severity: normal — on a tenant with sends that carry no company link, a full run silently under-counts the account table, the clicked sends and the program list, and nothing but one reconciliation check says so. No user reaches it yet (unmerged; no skill calls the script), and V1's failure holds the merge.
What: every `rp run` that names a lookup `fieldPath` (`PATH.company`, `PATH.person`) as a group-by or an aggregate drops, on the server, every row whose lookup is null: they come back neither as a null group nor in the count. The adapter assumes the opposite (the plan's "a row with no company link gets its own bucket", T-10's `no-company-link` row, the stand-in CLI's behaviour), and S0 never measured it: S0 measured that a lookup path resolves real values and that a PLAIN null field comes back as a group with no `v`, not what a null LOOKUP does. Three consequences on run 2, measured:
  1. `account` (groups by the company path): the account table is short by exactly the sends with no company link. In all 561 program-months, template-table sent minus account-table sent equals that program-month's count of in-scope sends with `GsCompanyId IS_NULL` (one grouped read; 561 of 561 equal, 0 differ); 25 program-months differ, 24,863 sends, 2.3% of the window. `honesty.noCompanyLink.sent` reads 0 and no `no-company-link` row carries a send.
  2. `click-attr` (groups by the company path): of 1,220 clicked sends in selected programs (one grouped read), the snapshot attributes 806; the 414 missing are exactly the clicked sends with no company link. No check sees this: `clicked-within-delivered` cannot, and `honesty.clicks.clickedSends` reports the attributed count. Clicked counts and click rates are understated, and a template whose only clicks are on such sends reads `unknown` instead of `tracked`.
  3. `uniques-month` (counts through both paths) is the program total that `decidePrograms` resolves "programs with sends" from and that `templates-sum-to-program` compares against. A program whose EVERY send lacks a company link is absent from it, so it is never selected, never counted as deleted or unselected, and its sends are in no honesty field: one listed program, 730 sends in the window's template payloads, 16 clicked sends.
Repro: the VALIDATION ENG-2 run 2 line. Its summary reads `reconciled: false`, `templates-sum-to-program` and `accounts-sum-to-program` not ok, with examples where the template table exceeds the program total and the account table. Then one read: COUNT of `Gsid` on `email_log_v2` with the adapter's `logWhere` (Source, AddressType, the window's two ExecutedDate bounds) plus `GsCompanyId IS_NULL`, grouped by `SourceId` and month: each program-month's count equals its template-minus-account gap.
Expected: the class, as an invariant: no send leaves the snapshot without landing in a fact row or an honesty count. A lookup path may decide which account or person a send belongs to, never whether the send is counted. A falsifiable test that enumerates nothing: a stand-in CLI that drops every row whose lookup path is null from any call naming that path (the measured server behaviour), plus a fixture with sends lacking a company link, one program whose every send lacks it, and a clicked send among them; the oracle (a straight count of the fixture's rows) must equal the snapshot's template, account and clicked totals, and that program must be selected. Two shapes the fix can take (the builder's call): read the null-link sends with a separate `IS_NULL` call per family (measured working here: the operator, on this field, in a grouped call), or move selection and program totals to a call that names no lookup. Also on the builder's list: the stand-in CLI should claim only server behaviour that has been measured; F-471 and this section are both a stand-in answering a shape the server answers differently. No T-10 change: `no-company-link` already exists.
Fix: 2026-10-03 (builder, third S1 fix batch on feat/jo-dash-s1-facts, PR #36 unmerged) — Class, in one sentence, yours: a lookup decided whether a send was counted, where it may only decide which account or person the send belongs to. Both shapes you named were needed, one per consequence. (1) Program totals and selection moved to a call that names no lookup: a new family, `totals` (program by month, COUNT, nothing else), is what `decidePrograms` reads "programs with sends" from and what `templates-sum-to-program` compares against. A program whose every send lacks a company link is now selected like any other. (2) The distinct counts are each asked through their own lookup alone: the uniques calls took people and accounts in one call, which dropped the sends lacking EITHER link from both counts. They are now two calls each, one through the person lookup and one through the company lookup, so people is exact over the sends that have a person and accounts over the sends that have a company. (3) The sends with no company link are read by their own calls, `GsCompanyId IS_NULL`: `account-nolink` (program by month by the six flags) fills the `no-company-link` rows T-10 already had, and `click-attr-nolink` (the clicked-sends attribution without the company path) attributes their clicks; each has its internal-domain twin, since internal recipients are the sends most likely to have no company. (4) The same drop sat under the survey calls: rows no program owns never came back, so `honesty.responses.unattributed` read 0 by construction. One more call counts them (`AOParticipantId IS_NULL`). Cost: 11 more calls on a pull with two internal domains. Not changed, with the reason: `step-click` joins through the JO log's link to the delivery log, and a JO row with no such link has no send to attribute a click to; the participant counts are distinct counts through their own lookup alone. The stand-in CLI: it now drops every row whose lookup is null from any call that groups or aggregates through that lookup, which is your falsifiable test, and it turned 23 of the suite's checks red before the fix. Its header now says, for each behaviour, that it was measured; the one it still assumes without a measurement on a non-empty case is that DOES_NOT_CONTAINS keeps a null address (F-472's known limit; 0 such sends on this tenant). No T-10 change. What the tester does: /reload-plugins, then the re-run; V1 judges this.
Judge: the real server, in this session (Bradley offered the live token; reads only, every command through the adapter's gate; 2026-10-03). Two things were measured that the fix rests on. (a) The new shapes are accepted and answer: `totals`, both single-lookup uniques calls, `account-nolink`, `click-attr-nolink` and `resp-unattributed` each ended ok with the columns their readers read; over one closed month `totals` and the template call sum to the same number. (b) "Has a company link" and "`GsCompanyId IS_NULL`" are an exact partition of the sends: over the 13-month window, tenant-wide, all sends minus (sends counted through the company path plus sends with IS_NULL) = 0, and the same for clicked sends = 0; IS_NOT_NULL equals the count through the path, so no send points at a company that is gone. Without (b) the fix would have traded one silent loss for another. The judge of record is V1 at the re-run: `templates-sum-to-program` and `accounts-sum-to-program` read ok over the closed months, `honesty.noCompanyLink.sent` equals your direct IS_NULL count for the selected programs, and the program your round found unselected is in the snapshot. Offline: the oracle (a straight count of the fixture's rows) equals the template, account and clicked totals under a stand-in that behaves as the server does, with a program whose every send lacks the link and with clicked sends lacking it, internal and external.
Sibling sweep: every family in FAMILIES was read for a lookup path in a group-by or an aggregate. account and click-attr: given a no-link twin. uniques-month, uniques-window: one lookup per call. resp-month, resp-participants, resp-total (through the participant lookup): the dropped rows are the unattributed ones, now counted by resp-unattributed. step-click, participants-month, participants-window: left, reasons in the Fix note. totals, template, classes, sent-since, click-json, account-nolink, click-attr-nolink, step, account-names, resp-unattributed: no lookup. A suite check now refuses any delivery-log call that counts sends, or asks two distinct counts, through a lookup.

## F-482 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-04 (builder, at the S2 close-out; observed by the tester in the re-verification round @ hb-20261004-03 and recorded there as "noticed, not a finding"; logged on Bradley's call so it is not lost)
Severity: polish — the time is early by the length of the plan step and the gap before the pull (minutes on the walks so far); no count is affected
What: scripts/engagement.mjs fixes a run's pull time when the run's working directory is created: resolveParams stamps `pulledAt` and main writes it to `run.json`, and a resumed run keeps it by design. The snapshot's `meta.pulledAt`, every row's `pulledAt`, a live schedule row's `asOf` and the report's "Data pulled" line all read that one stamp. ## F-483 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-05 (tester, spot check @ hb-20261004-04 on feat/jo-dash-s4a-runtime; production tenant, reads only; met at VALIDATION section HLT-1 / DSH-1 / DSH-5, Y1)
Severity: polish — a pull planned before midnight and run after it is refused with a hint that does not apply; no data is wrong, no call is made, and `--today <the plan's date>` or a new `--run` recovers it
What: scripts/engagement.mjs writes `today` into a run's parameters when its directory is made (`run.json`), and the resume check compares every parameter but `pulledAt` and `timeZone`. `today` is read from the clock again on the next invocation, so once the date turns it differs, and `run` with the same `--run` and the same flags exits 1: "the run at … was started with different parameters — pass the same flags to resume it, or a new --run". The flags were the same. The email-engagement skill runs `plan` and then `run` with one `--run`, so a plan just before midnight and its run just after hits this; so would a resume after a token stop that crosses midnight. Same mechanism as F-482: the run directory fixes the run's clock at the plan's start, and not consistently (`pulledAt` is kept, `today` is re-read and compared).
Repro: `engagement.mjs plan --kb <slug> --run r <flags>` before midnight local time; after midnight `engagement.mjs run --kb <slug> --run r <the same flags> --out s.json`. Observed: exit 1, the message above, nothing fetched. Adding `--today <the plan's date>` resumes it (measured).
Expected: a resumed run keeps the day it was planned on, the way it keeps its pull time (or, at least, the refusal names the parameter that moved and the flag that restores it). Natural to fix with F-482, which already owns the run's clock and rides S3b.

Fix: 2026-10-07 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch, PR #43 unmerged) — Class, in one sentence: a parameter re-read from the environment on resume and compared as if it had been given. On resume, when `--today` is not given, the parameters are re-resolved with the run's own `today` (so the window, the incomplete-from day and a `--sent-since` date derive the same as at the plan) before the comparison; a `--today` given on purpose is still a different run. The refusal names the parameters that moved ("different parameters (today, window, incompleteFrom moved)") instead of "pass the same flags". One mechanism with F-482: the run directory's clock is the plan day plus the fact-call stamp, both kept.
Judge: the process check in test/engagement.mjs plans a run with --today one day, runs it with no --today on another (the real clock), and holds the snapshot's day to the plan's; and a --today given on purpose is refused naming the parameter. On a tenant: V2's Y16's second clause, when the round crosses midnight (as the spot check did).

Reported: 2026-10-05 (tester, spot check @ hb-20261004-04 on feat/jo-dash-s4a-runtime; production tenant, reads only; VALIDATION section HLT-1 / DSH-1 / DSH-5, Y1 and Y3, and section DSH-2, Z1 and Z7)

Fix: 2026-10-07 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch, PR #43 unmerged) — Class, in one sentence: failure text stored at the grain of the text. A categorised row keeps `message` = the label and gains `category`; the Other row has `category: "other"`, the count and no message. Participant failures: the reason field takes no filter on CLI 1.0.10 (measured: CONTAINS, DOES_NOT_CONTAINS and STARTS_WITH refused; `rp schema` declares it not filterable), so the part is the ruled fallback — one grouped call (COUNT of rows, SUM of occurrences, per program, tenant-wide) and the capped sample — with `meta.health.categories.participantFailures` reading `counted: false, reason: not-filterable` and a caveat; no row read beyond one page. Verdict: REOPENED 2026-10-08 (tester, S3b fix round 2 verdict, V3) @ hb-20261008-01. Reopened: 2026-10-08 (tester @ hb-20261008-01, S3b fix round 2 verdict) — THIRD reopen; NOT deferred, on Bradley's ruling. What passed, measured (Y1's flags, a full pull with no --previous: plan 17 calls, run 194 made + 18 reused, exit 0, every health part read): `withFailures` 64 equals the direct COUNT (IN the 195 selected programs, ModifiedAt GTE 2026-07-11 and LT 2026-10-09), 64 programs, every per-program count equal; `.window` equals `meta.health.dayWindow` (2026-07-11, endExclusive 2026-10-09); `.counts` names exactly those 64; all 25 picks have `failureSamples` rows (every page 100 rows, at most five kept per program), the other 39 named in `notSampled` with reason cap, the smallest pick above the largest unsampled; the 123 programs with month-only refusals are in neither list; the 25 sample calls carry the entry-window call's bounds, one program each, `--order-by [{"name":"OccurrenceCount","order":"DESC"}]` (each call's argv rebuilt from the fetch log through the adapter's own `buildQuery` and `rpRunArgv`). The redesign's own model holds: the dominant program's most-repeated page now carries the wording Bradley read in the UI, `Custom field contains Invalid value {null} for EMAIL data type`, on 76 of 100 rows. What failed: the split. That wording matches no `participantFailures` pattern. The shipped `no-email` pattern is `Recipient Email Address field contains Invalid value`, and the platform writes the name of the field the address came from before "contains Invalid value": `Recipient Email Address field` when the program maps the standard field, `Custom field` when it maps a custom one. Both spellings occur on this tenant (the first on five sampled programs, 38 rows, split `no-email` / `bad-address` as designed). So the dominant program's `failureSamples` row reads `category: null, kind: null` (engagement.mjs ~3209) and its `entrySamples` row reads `category: "other", kind: "program-error"` (~3198): one unmatched wording, two labels, neither the kind Bradley ruled for a null or invalid address (`bad-address`, 2026-10-08). The committed oracle cannot see it: the fixture's `NULL_EMAIL_REASON` is spelled with the shipped pattern's own field name. Bradley, verbatim: "i don't know wy null would be a nonetype, it should be an error type right? i don't understand why it wasn't classified that way"; then, on the literal-match reading: "ok - that's the feedback the builder needs then. you need to be speaking in the same terms. the 'dominant mp digest' as you say, that should also be classified as an error. it's possible more will pop up we haven't encountered yet - if we don't know what it is, it should be flagged as needing investigating at the very least - maybe worth giving feedbavk to the repo to be able to classify it". Class, in one sentence: an entry refusal's kind is decided by a literal substring that includes text the platform varies per program, and a wording no pattern matches gets no kind in one table and `program-error` in the other instead of being flagged as unclassified. A falsifiable test of the class: over a fixture whose refusal wordings vary the text the platform interpolates (the field name before "contains Invalid value", and whatever else a product wording carries per program), every wording of one meaning lands in one category; and a wording no pattern matches carries ONE label in every table and list — unclassified, needing investigation — never `null`, never `program-error`, never a business rule. Expected (Bradley, 2026-10-08): the custom-field null-address refusals classified as an error (kind `bad-address`, his ruling of the day on null and invalid addresses); an unknown wording flagged as needing investigation at the very least; a way for the repo to classify it once it has been read. Disposition: Bradley ruled NOT deferred (2026-10-08, in session: "don't defer"). Rule 5 and the born-this-release valve: the section already carries a `Redesign:` line and the entry-refusal classifier is a mechanism of this release, so the next FIXED owes a redesign naming the model it replaces, not another tune. Severity unchanged (normal).

Redesign: 2026-10-08 (builder, third reopen, with Bradley in session as the data expert; the model replaced: "a category matches the whole product sentence literally, and a wording no pattern matches defaults to null in one table and program-error in the other" — the entry-refusal classifier of the second redesign). Class, in one sentence: an entry refusal's kind is decided by a literal substring that includes text the platform varies per program, and a wording no pattern matches gets a default instead of an explicit state. Measured before building (production, reads only, six calls on Bradley's token: two `rp schema`, one `jo p list` page, two 2000-row `rp run` pages of the refusals over the day window with no program filter, most repeated first and newest first; raw payloads in the session's scratchpad, never the repo; shapes in dev/S3B-FIX-ROUND-BRIEF.md § Round 3): the reason field is a JSON-path field whose schema says filterable, groupable and sortable all false, so a server-side census of wordings is impossible and the sample stays the one view of the text; the null-address wording is a TEMPLATE, `<field label> field contains Invalid value {<value>} for <TYPE> data type`, live with THREE labels on this tenant (`Recipient Email Address field` on 122 rows of 4,000, `Custom field` on 2 — one of them refused 49,467 times — and `Manager Email Address field` on 2, a variant neither role had seen); every other wording on both pages matched a shipped category. Rulings taken in session (Bradley, 2026-10-08): a pattern names the invariant core of a product wording, never the text the platform fills in; a wording no pattern matches is ONE explicit state everywhere, treated as the most actionable (it raises the alarm when it is what keeps people out) and flagged as needing investigation, with a path to the shipped list; the split carries occurrences beside rows, and says it is a sample.
Fix: 2026-10-08 (builder, fourth fix, under the second Redesign; feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch, PR #43 unmerged) — Class, in one sentence: an entry refusal's kind was decided by a literal substring that included text the platform varies per program, and an unmatched wording got a default instead of a state. (1) `FAILURE_CATEGORIES.participantFailures`: `no-email` is replaced by `invalid-field-value` ("Invalid or missing value in a mapped field", kind bad-address — the 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08 rulings on a null or invalid address) whose pattern is the core `contains Invalid value`; the masked text keeps the label, so a reader sees which field. (2) A fourth kind, `unknown` (`UNKNOWN_KIND`), and the reserved category `unclassified` (`UNCLASSIFIED_CATEGORY`): a text no category matches carries category unclassified, kind unknown, expected false in `failureSamples` and in `entrySamples`, and the step remainder (text the shipped step list does not name) is unclassified/unknown too. The bounce "Other" row stays `other`: it is the counted remainder of a TENANT's list (an open world of mail-server text), where unclassified is a PRODUCT wording the shipped list does not know; the typedef states the difference. `validateCategories` refuses the kind and the id on a tenant's list, and `kindOf` never yields unknown for a category. (3) The lists: unknown is not a business rule, so it counts as unexpected at entry (the program kept from admitting anyone by such a wording reads Only refused participants arriving) and fires Step errors like a program error; `signals.entry.sample.unclassified`, `byKind.unknown` and `signals.steps.unclassified` carry the count. (4) `failureSamples` and `entrySamples` rows gain `occurrences` — the refusals in all behind the `count` / `participants` rows, read from the page's OccurrenceCount — and the `failure-samples-sampled` caveat says so. (5) A new caveat, `unclassified-wordings`, counts the wordings, programs, participants and occurrences (and the step remainder) and names the remedy: read the texts in `failureSamples` (terminal only) and report them with /gs-superadmin:report-bug so the shipped list learns them, or add them to the tenant's --failure-categories file. Sibling cases the tester did not list: a field label never seen lands in the category by construction (the fixture cycles three; a fourth would too); a row stored before kinds (category null) reads unclassified in the lists, never a business rule; a STEP wording no category knows (the fixture's p-steperr: one participant) is named by Step errors. Typedef, pin and golden moved together; `schemaVersion` stays 1. The oracle now spells the null-address wording with three labels (`NULL_EMAIL_REASONS`) and carries a fictional unknown refusal (`UNKNOWN_REASON`) and an unknown step wording (`UNKNOWN_STEP_REASON`).
Judge: the fixture oracle (the sampled split per program equals a straight count of the fixture's refusals by the category the oracle assigns their kind, written by hand: three labels → one category, the unknown wording → unclassified) and the contract pin (category and kind never null; `(category === "unclassified") === (kind === "unknown")`; occurrences ≥ count); on a tenant, V4's Y2 as re-banked (the dominant program's `Custom field` wording under invalid-field-value / bad-address, Bradley reads the split, and every wording labelled unclassified is read by him and reported).
Mutation copy-out — sweep (source: the decision points of this redesign in scripts/engagement.mjs and scripts/engagement-query.mjs; a vacuity check on the committed checks, not closure); predictions written to a scratch file before the first run, four of the round's eight mutants, run over test/engagement.mjs one mutant at a time, the file restored byte for byte after each:
    M5 the null-address pattern spelled with the standard field's label again                       KILLED pred:KILL (three labels → one category; the chronic split)
    M6 an unmatched sample text reads category other / kind program-error again                      KILLED pred:KILL (unclassified / unknown in failureSamples and entrySamples; the contract pin)
    M7 step errors fire on program-error only (an unknown step wording no longer an error)           KILLED pred:KILL (p-steperr's byCategory and steps.unclassified)
    M8 validateCategories accepts kind unknown and the id unclassified on a tenant's list            KILLED pred:KILL (both suites)
  All as predicted.
Sibling sweep: batched — normal; the other readers of a sample or step row (S4b's health views, the report's --health section) do not exist yet; the dashboard page's `pageSnapshot` still empties the samples and embeds no text (the page suite); the dashboard runtime's reason ids are unchanged (unclassified is a category and unknown a kind, neither a reason).
Pass bar (stated before measuring, from the Judge line and VALIDATION Y2 as re-banked for V4): on the V4 pull, the dominant program's `failureSamples` row for `Custom field contains Invalid value {null} for EMAIL data type` reads category invalid-field-value, kind bad-address, with `occurrences` far above `count`, and its `entrySamples` row the same category and kind; no `failureSamples` or `entrySamples` row carries category null, kind null or `other`; every row that reads unclassified reads kind unknown in both tables and is counted in the `unclassified-wordings` caveat and in its program's `signals.entry.sample.unclassified`; Bradley reads the dominant program's split and every unclassified wording (none is expected unless the tenant carries a wording this session's two 2000-row pages did not).
Verdict: VERIFIED 2026-10-09 (tester, S3b fix round 3 verdict, V4) @ hb-20261008-02. Under test: feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch (PR #43 to dev, unmerged), clean and level with origin at ceca718; canary hb-20261008-02 in session; plugin link resolves to the working tree. Production tenant, confirmed by Bradley before the first call; reads only, one gs-admin call at a time. The V4 pull was the email-engagement skill's plan then run, with Y1's flags, full, no --previous: exit 0, 196 calls made + 20 reused, none failed. Pass bar, item by item. (1) Every structural arm of V3 holds. `withFailures` 64 equals a direct COUNT grouped by program over the day window and the selected programs: 64 programs, 63 per-program counts equal and one +4. The direct count ran about 40 minutes after the pull, and a narrow count of that program's refusals modified that day returned exactly 4 (accrual inside an open window). One window object serves the count and all 25 sample calls, one program each; 25 of 25 picks have rows; every page is non-increasing in occurrences. (2) The dominant program's `failureSamples` row for `Custom field contains Invalid value {null} for EMAIL data type` reads category `invalid-field-value`, kind `bad-address`, with `occurrences` about 650 times `count` (order 10^4 against order 10^1). Its `entrySamples` row carries the same category, kind and counts. (3) The `Recipient Email Address field` spelling (6 programs) and the `Manager Email Address field` spelling (1 program) land in the same category in both tables. (4) No participant-failure row in `failureSamples` or `entrySamples` (order 10^2 each) carries category null, kind null or `other`; `occurrences` >= `count` on every row. (5) Unclassified <=> unknown in both tables. 0 participant-failure rows read unclassified, so no `signals.entry.sample.unclassified` is set and no program is on Only refused participants arriving for one. (6) Bradley read the dominant split, verbatim: "that seems right". Beyond the builder's expectation ("none is expected"): the `unclassified-wordings` caveat fired on 28 wordings in 25 programs, order 10^3 sampled participants, and every wording is from the BOUNCE part's samples. All 124 bounce sample rows read `unclassified` / `unknown` (null / null at V3), and none matches the tenant's 30 bounce patterns. A step remainder of order 10^2 participants also counts, all in months before the period (Step errors 0, consistent). Bradley read all 28, verbatim: "in 1-22 those are all variations of bad address erros, same with 23-28". I first recommended a reopen on the typedef's line (engagement-query.mjs ~293: "other" is a tenant list's counted remainder, "unclassified" a PRODUCT wording; "The two are never the same thing"), because the bounce remainder reads `other` in the bounce table and `unclassified` in the samples. Bradley: "did we or did we not intentionally have a 'new errors are flagged as unknown' and this fills the brief? i haven't seen these before, but they are obviously bad email errors. isn't this working as intended?" It is. Ruling 12 (a wording no category knows is one explicit state, flagged for investigation) is the spec of record; the recommendation rested on the typedef's narrower gloss and was withdrawn. Bradley: "I think what we can do, is add these to our known 'bad-address' list, and maybe add a backlog item to see if there's a better way to intelligently flag novel error messages. we'll never get them all, and we can't keep re-opening this as an issue when a new one pops up." Done in the workspace (the tenant's category file, never the repo): 25 categories added, each an invariant core, plus one existing pattern trimmed to its core. 0 pattern overlaps; on order 10^3 raw bounce sample texts from every run directory, 0 texts match two categories and 0 texts lose a match. Residual, report only, not a bar item: the bounce remainder's two labels (`other` in the table, `unclassified` in the samples), and the caveat's report-bug remedy, which cannot teach a shipped bounce list that is empty by design (its tenant-file remedy can).

## F-485 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-05 (tester, spot check @ hb-20261004-04 on feat/jo-dash-s4a-runtime; no gs-admin call; VALIDATION section DSH-2, Z1 and Z7)
Severity: polish — the page is built correctly; the size report and its warning mislead whoever decides how to make a page smaller
What: scripts/dashboard-page.mjs `buildPage` fills the report's `rows` from the members of `facts` that are packed tables at the top level (`typeof t?.n === "number"`), so the five health tables, which sit one level down under `facts.health`, never appear. On the admin page over Y1's snapshot they are nearly all of 8 MB, and the report lists four small tables. The warning is fixed text, "Narrow the programs or the window, or turn customer lists off": on that page customer lists are already off and the Health tab, whose data makes the size, is not named.
Repro: `dashboard-page.mjs --spec <a saved spec with the admin page's Health tab on> --snapshot <a --health snapshot> --out-dir <dir>`; read `pages[0].rows` and `pages[0].warning` in the printed summary.
Expected: the size report counts every packed table the page embeds, the health five included (the As-shipped note says each is packed), and the warning names what is actually large, from that same report.
Fix: 2026-10-05 (builder, on feat/jo-dash-s4a-runtime) — Class, in one sentence: the size report read the top level of `facts` as the whole, when a packed table can sit one level down. `buildPage` now walks every member of the page's embedded `facts` at any depth and records each packed table's rows AND bytes (`report.tables`, with `report.rows` kept as the flat view: `health.bounceReasons` and its four siblings included). The warning and the refusal are built from that same report: they name the two largest tables with their megabytes, and the remedy follows from where the bytes are (a `health.*` table largest → "The Health tab's data makes the size: turn the tab off for this page, or narrow the programs or the window"; `byAccount` largest → customer lists; else narrow the programs or the window). No fixed text names a setting that is already off. ## F-491 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-07 (tester, S3b verdict round @ hb-20261007-02 on feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch; production tenant, reads only; VALIDATION section HLT-1 / DSH-1 / DSH-5, Y6 as re-banked)
Severity: normal — on a real tenant every alarm list the silent rules produce reads false to the admin: every live read says "Schedule run failed" for schedules that run daily as expected, and finished one-off campaigns read "No recent sends"
What: the cadence-aware silent rules (HLT-1, S3b: `judgeSilence`, the capped live `jo p describe` read, `silentPrograms(...).lists`) read a program's SCHEDULE as its SEND cadence and a DEFAULT as a run result. Class, in one sentence: the rules infer when a program should send, and whether its last run failed, from schedule metadata that on this tenant describes participant ingest and carries no run result. Instances, one pull (Y1's snapshot at 30 days): (1) "Schedule run failed" holds all 25 programs read live (the cap; 31 flagged): on every live-read schedule `lastRunSuccess` is false while `lastSuccessTime`, `lastFailureTime` and `failingSince` are all 0 — no run result is recorded at all, and false is the default; the KB rows never read true either (order 10^2 false, order 10^1 null). Bradley checked two in the Gainsight UI: each runs daily as expected; its recent participants failed only because they were already in the program — "not what I would describe as failing". (2) Two of the 25 have a schedule whose end time passed 78 days ago, and read "Schedule run failed" (Y6's bar: an ended schedule must not read as broken). (3) The schedules are almost all daily (`1/1`) participant-ingest crons: a run that admits nobody sends nothing, and the rule expects a send after every due day, so "Possible silent failure" lists a program that the settled picks record as sending once a month on the 1st, six days after its send; a program Bradley says runs monthly by design but takes participants quarterly is judged monthly. (4) "No recent sends" lists three programs that Bradley reads as finished one-off campaigns left Active; the "One-time and ad-hoc programs" list is empty, so the rule has no way to tell a finished campaign from a late one. Measured besides: a direct program x day read of the last 90 days for two programs on the run-failed list matches the snapshot's last send day and shows no later send — the last-send data is right; the lists' labels are wrong.
Repro: Y1 as run (`engagement.mjs plan`, then `run`, `--health --kb <slug>` and the round's inputs); `silentPrograms(snapshot, {days: 30}).lists` from engagement-query.mjs over the snapshot (a node one-liner); in the run directory, parse each `schedule-describe` payload's `data.advancedOutreach.participantSourceConfigurations[].scheduleInfo` (a JSON string) and read `schedules[]`: `lastRunSuccess`, `lastSuccessTime`, `lastFailureTime`, `failingSince`, `startTime`, `endTime`.
Expected: a run result is read only where one is recorded (`lastRunSuccess` false with every run time 0 is "no run result recorded", never "failed"), and a schedule past its end time reads ended; send silence is judged against what the program actually sends, not against the ingest cron. Two reads from this round the redesign can use, shapes only: the describe's schedule objects carry `startTime` and `endTime` (epoch-millisecond numbers) and the run-state fields above; `ao_participant_source_configuration` is reportable tenant-wide and holds `LastSyncedOn` (DATETIME) per participant source, with `AdvancedOutreachId` (STRING), `GsAdvancedOutreachId` (LOOKUP), `ParticipantSourceType` (STRING) and `ActiveVersion` (BOOLEAN) — evidence that an ingest ran, independent of sends (no success or failure field; `participant_criteria_step_execution` was read too and holds branch evaluations, not runs). Which signal decides "stopped working" is Bradley's ruling (the HLT-1 ruling 3 this implements) before a fix; the falsifiable test is his read of each list on the next pull.
Redesign: 2026-10-07 (builder, with Bradley in session as the data expert; the model replaced: "a program's schedule is its send cadence and a default is a run result" — the cadence-aware rules of HLT-1 ruling 3 of 2026-10-04, with the capped live describe read). Ruled first (the plan, HLT-1, "Rulings (Bradley, 2026-10-07)"): "stopped working" is four conditions, each read from its own data, never inferred from the schedule — the schedule ended or its sync is disabled; it runs but admits nobody; the only participants arriving are refused for a reason NOT expected by design; the program errors (a participant who got in falls off at a step). Measured before building (production, reads only, the shapes in dev/S3B-FIX-ROUND-BRIEF.md): the sources object holds `LastSyncedOn` on every Active program (the heartbeat: 27 of 64 synced within a day), the schedule run-state fields are unset even on a program that synced that day, `ao_participants` carries `CreatedAt`/`ModifiedAt` and a filterable step-failure reason, the refusal object's `ModifiedAt` moves when the same key is refused again, stale programs have NO schedule (synced once at creation), REVIEW participants sit on drafts, and the server's CONTAINS is case-insensitive.
Fix: 2026-10-07 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch, PR #43 unmerged) — Class, in one sentence: the rules inferred when a program should send, and whether its last run failed, from schedule metadata that describes participant ingest and carries no run result. Replaced by `programHealth` (alias `silentPrograms`; `judgeHealth` over plain inputs) in engagement-query.mjs: six signals per program, each from its own table with a "cannot tell" state where the table was not read — schedule (recurring, ended by its end date, not started, one-time, none, disabled by the list's flag), ingest (the newest active source's last sync against the cron's last due day: on-schedule, overdue, never-synced, cannot-judge, cadence-unreadable, stopped, one-time), admissions (participants created over the last `--quiet-due-days` due days, default 5; too few due days in the window is never an alarm), entry (exact refusals over the window with the sampled split by the shipped expected list), steps (step failures counted server-side by category per month — a step's action failed, the platform error state, a bounce drop and a record delete, the last two expected), sends (the program's OWN history for every program; the ingest cron says nothing about sends), and finished (a one-off with no participant ACTIVE or PAUSED). ONE list per program by precedence (`HEALTH_LISTS`): schedule-ended, sync-disabled, ingest-overdue, failing-entries, admitting-nobody, step-errors, finished, no-recent-sends, no-sends-in-window, cannot-judge, ok. The four instances the tester listed: (1) no run result is ever read from the schedule fields; (2) an ended schedule reads ended; (3) the monthly sender on a daily cron reads ok by its history; (4) finished campaigns left Active read finished when nothing is in flight. New tables `sources`, `admissions`, `entryFailures`, `stepFailures`, `entrySamples` (additive; typedef, pin and goldens moved together; `schemaVersion` 1); the live `jo p describe` reads are RETIRED (`HEALTH_DESCRIBE_CAP` gone; a run that logged them still reduces). Cost on the measured tenant: four tenant-wide calls plus the per-program samples against 25 describes retired.
Judge: Bradley's read of each list on the next pull (Y6 as re-banked) and the signals tenant in the fixture — one program per list, each list's cause written by hand (an ended schedule, a disabled flag, a sync older than the last due day, zero admissions over five due days with expected refusals, the same with the unexpected null-address refusal, a CTA-step failure and a platform error this month, a one-off with every participant completed); Y17 holds the heartbeat to the UI's last run; Y18 holds the step categories to direct counts.
Mutation copy-out — sweep (source: the decision points of the redesign in scripts/engagement-query.mjs; a vacuity check on the committed checks, not closure); predictions written to a scratch file before the first run, the other four of the round's eight mutants, run over test/engagement.mjs one mutant at a time:
    M1 judgeHealth: on-schedule when synced ON the due day (>=) → strict (>)  KILLED pred:KILL
    M2 judgeHealth: a schedule has ended when its end day is before as-of → after  KILLED pred:KILL
    M6 judgeHealth: failing-entries fires on an unexpected refusal → on expected-only  KILLED pred:KILL
    M8 provisionalSpan: the flags-from day clamped to the incomplete-from day → never clamped  SURVIVED pred:SURVIVE (no committed check has the re-pull horizon later than the incomplete-from day; a vacuity to note for V2's read of a 1-month re-pull, not a defect)
  All as predicted (7 killed, 1 predicted survivor).

The section carries a `Redesign:` line, so this reopen is of the model, not a tune.
Reopened: 2026-10-08 (tester @ hb-20261007-03, S3b fix-round verdict) — first reopen since the Redesign. Counts, order 10^1 Active programs judged: schedule-ended order 10^1 (35), sync-disabled 0, ingest-overdue 0, failing-entries 0, admitting-nobody 1, step-errors 6, no-recent-sends 2, finished order 10^1 (10), no-sends-in-window 0, cannot-judge 0, ok order 10^1 (11). Read TRUE by Bradley: admitting-nobody ("this does read true - in this case i know why no one is getting in. we stopped bringing in this customer type into the system. so it makes sense, and good to flag in either case, maybe i didn't know that"); finished, all of it ("those all look one and done yes"); ok, all of it (one program's newest refusal is a null address the sample cap left unread: F-484); no-recent-sends 1 of 2 ("it does look like [that program] is broken somehow. so that tracks"); schedule-ended 20 of 35 (every schedule the program carries has ended; "if the schedule was over, i would aggree"). Read FALSE: (1) schedule-ended 15 of 35. Each carries TWO schedule objects on one daily cron: the participant sync (`jobType` ADVANCED_OUTREACH_BIONIC_QUERY) ending years ahead, and a job schedule (ADVANCED_OUTREACH_SCHEDULE, a ONE-TIME job context) that ended years ago. `pickSchedule` (engagement.mjs ~2420) keeps the shortest-period recurring schedule and breaks the tie by position, so it reads the ended job schedule; the schedule signal then outranks the program's own heartbeat (ingest reads `stopped` on a source that synced that morning; 15 of the 35 sent within 30 days). Bradley's UI read of one: "Scheduled to sync from 5th May 2025 to 6th May 2030 at 9:30 am America/Los_Angeles Daily ... I saw it last run this morning at 9:30am pacific more or less. if the schedule was over, i would aggree, but this one is still going"; a live `jo p describe` the same day shows its participant source carrying ONLY the participant-sync schedule (ending 2030) and a `lastSyncedOn` that morning, so the KB doc (as of 2026-09-10) holds the job schedule besides, and the reader chose it. (2) step-errors 6 of 6. Each is on the list only through Send Email delivery drops the shipped step list does not name (`Email is Reject, participant is dropped from process at step 'Send Email'`; `Sending email failed with errors Email Failed: Recipient on Gainsight bounce list at step Send Email`; `... Recipient has opted out at step Send Email`), read by a direct `rp run` of one program's uncategorised step text (order 10^2 rows, all DROP). Bradley ruled the model in session (2026-10-08): THREE kinds, not two — business rules (already in list, unique criteria, advanced criteria, unsubscribed, Global Opt Out, the Send Email opt-out; "i do agree record delete is a business rule, if an odd one"), bad-address errors ("bounced is merely an 'expected' error, in the sense that if their email is bad we would expect it to bounce. again, it's not the same as 'participant with unique criteria exists' type thing"; "how does someone get on a bounce list? by their email bouncing right? aren't those basically the same?"; bounce, bounce list, reject, `Bounced recipient(to) email ... in Step 'Send Email'` and the null or invalid address wordings: "yes, they should be in type 2"), and program errors (a step's action failed; platform error). The shipped `expected` boolean holds two kinds: `bounce-drop` (the builder's choice) and `bounce-list` (ruling 2 of 2026-10-07) sit with the business rules, and reject and the Send Email twins fall to "other", which the list reads as a program error. (1) `judgeHealth`: a program with no doc reads `schedule.state` `undocumented` and a pull made without a KB `unknown` (told apart by `kbSource`, from `honesty.kb`); either makes the ingest `cannot-judge` with `why` `no-doc` or `no-kb` (both in `CANNOT_JUDGE_REASONS`), neither is ever a one-off for Finished (`oneOff` is now a DOCUMENTED one-time or no-schedule), and the list reads Cannot judge yet BEFORE the send history is read as late — whether a quiet program is a finished one-off or a stalled recurring one is exactly what the schedule tells apart. The alarms a program's own data supports (Step errors, No sends in the window) still fire. (2) A documented program the list says was modified after its doc's as-of date is judged from the doc and flagged (`signals.schedule.docBehind`, with `asOf` and `modifiedAt`): a platform event bumps every program's modified date at once (the refresh skill's own warning), so the doc is not discarded on that ground. `dimensions.programs[].modifiedAt` (additive) carries the list's date. (3) `honesty.kb` — `{source, undocumented: [ids], behind: [{programId, asOf, modifiedAt}]}` from the one function `kbGap` — and the caveat `kb-behind-tenant`, which counts both sets and names the remedy. (4) `plan` prints `estimate.kb` (source, undocumented, behind, unlisted, programs, refreshSeconds at one describe each, keysFile, listFile) and writes the narrow refresh's inputs beside plan.json: `kb-gap-keys.json` (the manifest keys) and `kb-gap-list.json` (the list rows of the undocumented programs, in the list's own envelope, what `manifest upsert-batch --partial` registers); a program the list itself lacks is counted apart (`unlisted`) — it has no row to register. (6) The run directory's KB copy (`kb-steps.json`) carries the KB manifest's stamp (size and mtime) and is read again when the stamp moved, so a run after that refresh judges from the refreshed KB, never from the plan's copy. Cost: zero tenant calls on the pull; the refresh is priced and chosen. Reported: 2026-10-07 (tester, S3b verdict round @ hb-20261007-02 on feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch; production tenant, reads only; VALIDATION Y2)

What: the message mask leaves two kinds of value in `facts.health.failureSamples`. (1) A mail gateway's bracketed message id is masked to `<id>` when it is alphanumeric, but not when it contains `-` or `_`: in one page of bounce samples, three such ids came through verbatim beside order-10^1 siblings that read `<id>`. (2) Recipient mail-server host names are kept (an organisation's mail host, a relaying server's domain), which names the recipient's organisation. Class, in one sentence: the id rule's character class is narrower than the ids the gateways write, and host names are not a masked kind. The masking search Y2 runs (addresses, five-digit runs, IPv4) cannot see either, so both passed it.
Repro: Y1's snapshot; group `facts.health.failureSamples` by message and read the bracketed tails of the gateway-blocked rows (a bracket holding a mixed-case token with `-` or `_` and a short region suffix), and the rejections whose text begins with a host name.
Expected: the id rule masks a token with `-` and `_` the way it masks an alphanumeric one; whether host names are masked (to `<host>`) or left for the categories to cut is the builder's call with Bradley (ruling 5 chose categories over a wider mask for local addresses). A fixture row of each kind pins it.
Fix: 2026-10-07 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch) — Class, in one sentence: the id rule's character class was narrower than the ids the gateways write, and host names were not a masked kind. The token rule's class is now letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, `+`, `/`, `=` (12 or more, a letter and a digit, bounded by look-arounds instead of word boundaries, so a dotted or base64-style id is one token), and a new `host` rule (dotted labels ending in a top-level domain of letters) masks a mail host to `<host>` — the builder's call: a host names the recipient's organisation, and unlike the local-address gap this kind the mask CAN see (ruling 5 chose categories where it could not); Bradley may overrule at the verdict. Six rules, in order: email, uuid, ipv4, host, token, number. Fixture rows of each kind pin it (a mail host; a gateway id with dots, hyphens and underscores; a base64-style id).
Judge: the MASKS table — every rule has a case it is the first to change — plus the standing "what diagnoses the failure is kept" case (SMTP codes, enhanced status codes, short numbers untouched).
Sibling sweep: batched — polish; the one other masker is the same function (reduce's second pass).
Pass bar (stated before measuring, from the Judge line and the kickoff): the masked text captured at hb-20261007-02, run through the shipped mask (MASK_RULES, six rules), leaves no host name and no hyphen or underscore id; Bradley may overrule the builder's call that hosts are masked.

## F-494 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-07 (tester, S3b verdict round @ hb-20261007-02 on feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch; KB read only; met while preparing VALIDATION Y14)

Expected: a CRON-type schedule with no readable cron is recurring with the cron unknown (or `recurring` null with the reason stated), never false; a fixture doc of that shape pins it.
Fix: 2026-10-07 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch) — Class, in one sentence: a pass-through classification label read as a boolean trait. Fixed at the reader, not the shipped parser: `programTraits.recurring` is true for "recurring", false for "one-time" and "no schedule captured", and null (unknown) for any pass-through label ("CRON", "unknown"), so such a program is Ungrouped by a recurring rule rather than "not recurring"; the suggestion input's note says so. The audit report's type column is unchanged.
Judge: the groups suite's check over a doc of that shape (classification "CRON", cron null → null; "one-time" → false; "recurring" → true).
Sibling sweep: batched — polish; the only other reader of the classification as a boolean was the retired cadence rule (judgeHealth reads it as a state).
Pass bar (stated before measuring, from the Judge line and the kickoff): a CRON-type program with no readable cron reads `recurring` null (Ungrouped) in dashboard-groups' suggestion input, never false.
Verified: 2026-10-08 (tester, S3b fix-round verdict, V2 @ hb-20261007-03, feat/jo-dash-s3b-health-batch at 244b0dc, canary hb-20261007-03 in session; no gs-admin call) — RE-VERIFICATION, the bar above. The KB holds order 10^0 programs whose only schedules are CRON-type with no cron; none sent in the window, so none is selected. A copy of the previous round's snapshot had one selected program's schedule replaced by that real KB shape (classification `CRON`, cron null): `suggest-input` reads its `recurring` null; `resolve` with the previous round's recurring spec moves it Recurring -1, Ungrouped +1, Not recurring unchanged. Verified: 2026-10-12 (tester, S5-V first sitting @ hb-20261011-02, the branch at dee1403; production, reads only) — the Judge's live half, VALIDATION § F-502 / F-503 / F-504 K1 and K2, over the round's fast-path snapshot: the Schedule ended list is EMPTY where V2 had 29 rows; 68 programs carry `oneRunWindow: true` (V2's count), all classified one-time; 30 of them (Active, ended, nobody in flight) sit on Finished campaign with the Why ending "(one-day schedule, ended <day>)", the other 38 Paused or Stopped and unjudged, none on any alarm list; the grouping trait reads recurring for exactly the 12 one-run programs that sent in two or more months (Bradley's hand-fed program, named in session, is one of them and resolves to Recurring) and not recurring for the other 56, which resolve to One-off. The two-day case stays unmeasured on this tenant (Bradley knows none; the fixture program p-twoday is its only measurement): a blind spot, not a reopen.
Severity: normal — the Health tab's alarm list and the Recurring / One-off grouping are wrong for an admin on a tenant that schedules one-off sends as a daily cron boxed into one day (68 of this tenant's 127 "recurring" programs are that shape)
What: `pickSchedule` / `classifySchedule` read the cron expression alone. A daily cron whose documented window (start to end) spans a single day can fire exactly once, yet it classifies recurring: at refresh the program lands in the Recurring supergroup, and once its day has passed with no sync since, on the Schedule ended alarm list (29 rows this pull, 14 of them one family of one-and-done campaigns) while an otherwise identical campaign run by hand, with no schedule documented, reads Finished campaign (5 rows). Bradley asked what separates the two; the answer is how the builder scheduled it, not its health. The V4 ruling (F-491, 2026-10-09) left ended one-run windows on the alarm list because intent cannot be read; this is the narrower, data-deterministic part: the window's capacity.
Repro: over the round's snapshot, `programHealth(snapshot, {days: 30}).lists["schedule-ended"]` holds 29 programs whose `dimensions.programs[].schedule` is `recurring` with `endTime - startTime` under one day on a daily cron; `lists.finished` holds 5 with `no schedule captured`.
Expected: a schedule whose window admits exactly one run (end minus start shorter than one cron period) classifies one-time; when it has ended and no participant is still active or paused, the program reads Finished campaign with a row note "one-day schedule, ended <day>" so the shape stays visible; a window admitting two or more runs keeps alarming on Schedule ended when it ends (Bradley's hard-to-spot case: meant recurring, window set for about two days). The grouping trait `recurring` follows the same classification; a program re-run through repeated one-day windows (sends in two or more months) is Bradley's hand-fed case, read as recurring by hand, which the builder should keep out of One-off (the F-491 taxonomy's hand-fed class). LTR-11's acknowledgement stays for what the data cannot tell.
Fix: 2026-10-11 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261011-02) — Class, in one sentence: the classification read the cron alone, never the window's capacity. pickSchedule now reads a recurring schedule whose window is shorter than one cron period (end minus start) as a ONE-RUN window: the program classifies one-time, marked `oneRunWindow` (additive on T-10's program dimension; the latest end among such windows decides); a one-run window beside a live recurring schedule leaves the program recurring; a window at least one period long (Bradley's two-day case) stays recurring and keeps alarming Schedule ended. The health signal carries the window's end, so the row reads "one-day schedule, ended <day>" beside Finished campaign (ended with nobody in flight). The grouping trait follows the classification, except a program re-run through one-day windows that sent in two or more months: the hand-fed class, read as recurring (programTraits reads the months from the snapshot's sends). The acknowledgement for what the data cannot tell stays (LTR-11).
Judge: the adapter suite's F-502 pickSchedule check and its lists check over the three new signals programs (p-oneday Finished with the note, p-twoday Schedule ended, p-rerun Finished and one-run), the grouping suite's F-502 traits check, the page suite's health-silent check (two Schedule ended rows; the one-day note in the Finished list) and the contract's schedule pin (oneRunWindow a boolean)

## F-503 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-10 (tester, V2 first sitting @ hb-20261010-01 on dev; no tenant call; VALIDATION Z5 and D2)
Verified: 2026-10-12 (tester, S5-V first sitting @ hb-20261011-02; no tenant call) — K3 over the built admin page and a scratch build with the Templates tab off: every copy line is concrete (`accounts.pull=true`, `sources.0.params.stepDetail=true`, `sources.0.params.internalDomains=`, `pages.0.tabs.2.enabled=true`), no `[]` anywhere; each accepted and priced by `change --dry-run` (pull, pull, pull with a value, rebuild both ways for the Templates tab; Health off prices pull by the adapter's refresh rule); the bracketed control `pages[].tabs[].enabled=true` refused with the writer's own list message, never "not a field path".
Severity: normal — the line a page tells an admin to copy for a list-nested setting cannot be run as written
What: the shared lacks plumbing builds the copy line from the LACKS row's setting path, which for a setting inside a list is the SPEC_DESCRIPTIONS covers path with empty brackets: the Steps panel's notice reads `… change <slug> sources[].params.stepDetail=true` and an offered Templates tab's `… change <slug> pages[].tabs[].enabled=true`. Neither names a source, a page or a tab, and neither matches the spec writer's own path grammar, which is dotted with indexes (`sources.0.params.stepDetail`), so even S5's `change` verb could not take them. The top-level `accounts.pull=true` line is fine. Z0 (2026-10-05) ruled the copy line a deterministic command.
Repro: build the admin page over any snapshot without step detail; read the Steps panel's notice; or turn the Templates tab off and open it.
Expected: the line carries the concrete path for the page and tab the notice stands on (`pages.0.tabs.2.enabled=true`, or the ids the `change` verb will accept), in the writer's grammar; a test holds every emitted copy line to a path `validate` accepts.
Fix: 2026-10-11 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261011-02) — Class, in one sentence: the copy line carried the descriptions' KIND path where the writer's grammar wants a concrete one. The runtime's lackFacts writes the line through concretePath: `pages[]` becomes this page's index, `tabs[]` the offered tab's index in the spec's list (the page model carries page.index and each tab's index), `sources[]` the dashboard's source (sources.0), and a trailing `[]` is dropped so a list setting's line still ends at the = sign: pages.0.tabs.1.enabled=true, sources.0.params.stepDetail=true, sources.0.params.internalDomains=. The entry command's coveredPath reads the dotted grammar too (one normalisation for both grammars), so `change` with such a line prices it. The gs-path label beside the notice still shows the kind path (what the setting is); the line names the field.
Judge: the page suite's F-503 check — every copy line the built pages emit (and the About tab's internal-domain line) parsed back, set on a copy of its spec through setPath, no validation problem about that field, the entry command's cost table covering it — and the two existing lackFacts checks moved to the concrete lines
Reopened: 2026-10-12 (tester, S5-V second sitting @ hb-20261012-01; the real dashboard's built admin page; no tenant call) — the same class, a copy line that cannot be run as drawn: every line the pages emit (`… dashboard.mjs refresh <slug>`, the `change <slug> …` lines, the About tab's How to refresh) omits `--kb <folder>`, and in a workspace that holds two tenant KB folders (this one: production and the sandbox) the entry command refuses each as drawn: "this workspace holds 2 tenant KB folders (…) — pass --kb <the one this dashboard belongs to>" (measured on `change` this sitting; the skill prose itself says every dashboard verb takes `--kb` then). Expected: the page knows its KB folder (the spec's) and the copy lines carry `--kb <folder>` when the workspace holds more than one, or always; the README's refresh and scheduler recipes the same; the F-503 check runs each emitted line through the entry command in a two-KB fixture workspace.
Fix: 2026-10-12 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-fix2 merged into feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261012-02) — Class, in one sentence: the page did not know which knowledge-base folder it belonged to, so no line it drew could name it. The page model now carries `kb`, the folder's NAME (never a path: the spec may hold none, and a folder name is not one); the entry command passes `basename(kbDir)` to every page it builds, and the page-builder CLI takes `--kb <name>` or reads the folder from where the spec writer keeps a spec (`kbDirOfSpecFile`, the writer's own knowledge of its layout; a spec read from anywhere else gets no folder and stderr says the lines omit the flag). `COPY_LINES` take the folder and append `--kb <folder>` to every line they draw (`change`, `refresh`, `health`), always, so the How to refresh line, every notice's line and the health signal's line run as drawn in a workspace with two tenants; the README's recipes carry `--kb` on every dashboard line (the on-demand and health-only refreshes, the runner scripts, the change, the export and import), and the skill says every dashboard verb takes it always. The sibling the tester did not list: the health "Other" signal's terminal line, which carried no folder either; it takes it through the same constant.
Judge: the page suite's F-503 copy-line check extended: a page built from the writer's own layout (`<kb>/dashboards/<slug>/spec.json`) has every pre-rendered copy line end in `--kb <folder>` (the refresh line of How to refresh among them) and names the folder in the steps, the same page built with no folder known omits the flag, and an offered-tab build with the folder known has every notice line carry it; the entry-command suite's F-503 walk: a second tenant KB folder is added to the fixture workspace, every line the built admin page offers to copy is run from the workspace folder through the entry command as drawn (a `change` line as a dry run, the refresh and health lines for real), each exit 0, and the same refresh line without `--kb` is refused naming the two folders, as the tester saw.
Verified: 2026-10-13 (tester, S5-V third sitting @ hb-20261012-02, the branch at d364297; production, reads only) — I14 on the real workspace, which holds two tenant KB folders: the admin page offers three distinct command lines (`change <dash> sources.0.params.stepDetail=true`, `change <dash> pages.0.tabs.2.enabled=true`, `refresh <dash>`) plus the health signal's terminal line, every one ending in `--kb <folder>`; the page script's ENTRY_COMMAND constant is the only dashboard.mjs string without it. Each pasted as drawn into a terminal in the workspace folder: both change lines with `--dry-run` appended exit 0 and price (the step-detail flip "pull … about 72 minutes (about 2 logins of an hour)", the Templates tab "rebuild only (no pull)"); the refresh line ran for real as I10's resume (exit 0); the health line ran for real with its `<program id>` placeholder filled from the snapshot (exit 0, the program's health parts read from the last pull). None refused for the folder. The About tab's How to refresh names the folder (as the one that holds this tenant's knowledge-base folder), where to type the line, the login, the slash command, and what a pull longer than the login does. One note, no departure: the health line is drawn with the literal `<program id>` (the "Other" signal's line stands for every program), so it is the one copy line an admin edits before pasting; the bar allowed for it ("the refresh line for real, or the health line").

## F-504 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-10 (tester, V2 first sitting @ hb-20261010-01 on dev; production tenant, reads only; VALIDATION Y1 and D1)
Verified: 2026-10-12 (tester, S5-V first sitting @ hb-20261011-02; production, reads only, one plan) — K4: a plan with the two internal domains, the two test accounts and the tenant's category file (56 entries since V2.5) reads `estimate.health.categoryCalls.bounce` {categories 56, classes 6, calls 336, seconds 1008, secondsEach 3}; the failure-settings and tabs questions quote the cost in those words (56 × 6 recipient classes, about 17 minutes); R1, a Health refresh on one class, ran at 1.16× its `estimate.thisRun.seconds` and the resumed full at 1.28× on a slower afternoon, both inside 1.5× (V2 measured 2×). Note for the fix round: F-511 moves the category-cost quote to the tabs question; the K4 bar moves with it.
Severity: normal — a tenant that captures its bounce wordings (the ruled remedy for novel text) pays a refresh that approaches the token hour; unsure, so normal
What: the bounce categories are counted with one CONTAINS call per category per recipient class and span: with the tenant's 55-pattern file the plan priced 449 calls / 3473 s (95 s inside the token) and the run made 330 `health-bounce-cat` calls of its 443 (55 categories x 6 classes: all, two internal domains, test, two test-internal overlaps). V4's pull with 30 categories was 200 calls. R1 ruling 3 expected "about fifty calls a refresh". Also measured: the seconds estimate is 2x high (1757 s wall against 3473 s planned; the category calls take about 2.5 s, priced near 8), so `token.fits` turns false a long way before the pull would fail.
Repro: `plan --health --failure-categories <55-entry file> --test-account x2 --internal-domain x2 <common>` over a full program set; read `estimate.thisRun` and the fetch log's family counts after the run.
Expected: the per-category cost does not multiply by the class twins where it need not (one call per category grouped by a class dimension where the server allows it, or categories counted on the `all` class only with the class split carried from the uncategorised totals), or the plan says plainly that categories cost calls x classes and the interview shows it; and the per-call seconds for the category family are re-fitted from a measured pull. LTR-9's lever list is the home for the design.
Fix: 2026-10-11 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261011-02) — Class, in one sentence: a cost said nowhere, priced from a default. The plan's estimate.health.categoryCalls.bounce says plainly what the bounce categories cost: categories × recipient classes (all, each internal domain, the test accounts, the test accounts on each domain) = counted calls, with the seconds; the interview quotes it in the failure-settings and tabs questions, and the internal-domains and test-accounts asks say each adds a class, before any is added. The category call is priced at its measured 2.5 s (CALL_SECONDS health-bounce-cat = 3) instead of the 7 s default that priced the 55-category refresh at 3473 s against 1757 s wall. The calls are NOT cut: the exact cuts (the external complement in one DOES_NOT_CONTAINS call per category instead of one ENDS_WITH call per domain; a per-category class switch) each need a tenant measurement first and are recorded as LTR-9 levers 5 and 6 for Bradley's call.
Judge: the adapter suite's F-504 check (6 classes with two domains and a test account; calls = categories × classes on a first pull; 3 s a call; 1 class with no domain; 0 calls with no category file) and the entry-command suite's F-504 wording check

## F-505 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-10 (tester, V2 first sitting @ hb-20261010-01 on dev; no tenant call; Bradley driving the filters, VALIDATION Z3)
Severity: polish — the figures are right; the filter bar's program list and its count mislead the viewer about what they hold and how the other filters affect them
What: the line above the program list reads "195 of 195 selected" whatever months or statuses are chosen, and the summary says "195 programs shown" while the Programs table under a one-month filter lists far fewer rows (a kept program with no sends in the chosen months has no row). Nothing on the filter bar says the list is "every program that sent in the pulled window" (the instance holds about three times as many programs; the About tab says so). Bradley: "it's unclear what drives that 195 list, and how I can impact it"; he expected the list to respond to the month and status filters.
Repro: on the admin page pick one closed month; read the count line, the summary and the Programs table's row count.
Expected: the count line names the set ("N programs sent in this window") and the summary counts programs with rows under the current filters; programs with no sends in the chosen months, or outside the chosen statuses, are dimmed or hidden in the list. The layout wishes beside this (the list opening on click, the filters' grouping, Reset's placement, the two notices in the bar) are S4d's and are recorded in the plan, not here.
Fix: 2026-10-13 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-fix3 merged into feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261013-01) — Class, in one sentence: the filter bar's program list and its counts read the SELECTION where the viewer read the VIEW (the months and statuses in force). The count line names the set: "N programs sent in this window, M selected" (N the pulled set the About tab counts). The list's rows answer to the other filters without touching the selection: a program outside the chosen statuses is dimmed with "hidden by status", one with no send in the chosen months (under the recipient class in force) with "no sends in these months" — the rows are their own region (`proglist`) so a status box repaints them (the months already repaint the bar). The summary's "shown" counts the programs with rows under the filters, from the engine's one scope (`scope.programsWithRows`, additive on the result), and says "(K selected programs with no sends in these months)" when any kept program has none, so it agrees with the Programs table's row count; nothing changes when every kept program has rows. Dimmed, not hidden: a hidden row could not be deselected, and the search already hides. Sibling run against the fix: the leaders' page (every status by default, closed months) dims nothing on the fixture and its summary keeps "5 programs shown"; the 400-program fixture (half paused) dims 200 rows by status and still lists all 400.
Judge: the page suite holds the admin page's rows to the fixture (the paused program dimmed by status over the whole window; under one month the two programs with no send in it dimmed "no sends in these months", every row still selected), the summary under that month to "2 programs shown (2 selected programs with no sends in these months). 1 program hidden by status (showing Active)." and the whole window's to "4 programs shown." with no clause, the status change's commit to repaint the list region, and the count line's wording; the query suite's goldens carry `programsWithRows` (5, 2 and 1 across the cases). The tester's live arm: the real admin page under one closed month (§ DSH-3 fourth sitting).
Verified: 2026-10-13 (tester, S5-V fourth sitting @ hb-20261013-01; Bradley driving the filters on the rebuilt real admin page; no tenant call) — the count line "191 programs sent in this window, 191 selected" throughout. One closed month (September): "39 programs shown (152 selected programs with no sends in these months). 0 programs hidden by status (showing every status)", the no-send programs dimmed in the list, the Programs table's rows eyeballed at 39 (the page shows no row count). Reset: "191 programs shown." with no clause. Running now: "65 programs shown. 126 programs hidden by status (showing Active)". Reset clears every dim; 191 selected every time (no program deselected by a filter).

## F-507 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-10 (tester, V2 first sitting @ hb-20261010-01 on dev; production tenant, reads only; the skill walk's step 2)
Severity: polish — the skill can start a gap-fill that outlives the token after telling the user the pull fits
What: `estimate.token.fits` judges `estimate.thisRun.seconds` alone, and the skill's step 2 quotes `estimate.templates.seconds` beside it without adding them: this round the plan said the pull fits with 1298 s of token left while the gap-fill it then offered was priced at 834 s plus the 267 s pull (the tester asked for a re-login first). The KB re-documentation ask has the same shape (`estimate.kb.refreshSeconds`).
Repro: a plan on a token with less than the gap-fill plus the pull remaining; read `estimate.token.fits` and the ask's wording.
Expected: `fits` (or a second field the skill reads at the ask) accounts for the gap-fill and the re-documentation the plan proposes, and the ask says when the chosen budget would outlive the token.
Fix: 2026-10-13 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-fix3 merged into feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261013-01) — Class, in one sentence: the plan judged the login against the pull alone and the skill's asks quoted the proposals' seconds beside that judgment without adding them. The plan's `estimate.token` now carries, beside `fits` (the pull alone, unchanged so nothing that reads it moves), `afterPullSeconds` (what the login has left once the pull and its margin are made: the budget any gap-fill has to fit) and `withProposals {seconds, fits}` (the pull plus `kb.refreshSeconds` plus `templates.seconds`, and whether that fits the login); `estimate.templates.secondsEach` (the per-template fetch seconds) lets a partial budget be priced. The skill's two asks read them: the re-documentation ask says when `kb.refreshSeconds` is more than `afterPullSeconds`, with both in minutes, and that a login first makes room; the template ask fills without asking only when the count is 50 or fewer AND its seconds fit `afterPullSeconds`, otherwise prices each choice (all, the first 50, none: the count times `secondsEach`) against the budget and says which would outlive the login, offering the login first or a smaller budget. Sibling: the dashboard's refresh verb already added the re-documentation's seconds to its own budget (`redocSeconds`), so it was not the instance's path; unchanged.
Judge: the engagement suite plans on a login the pull just fits (5 s to spare) over the KB-gap fixture (five templates, 15 s) and holds `token.fits` true, `afterPullSeconds` 5, `withProposals.seconds` to the pull plus the KB and template seconds and `withProposals.fits` false, and on a roomy login both true. The tester's live arm: the skill's ask on a real plan (§ DSH-3 fourth sitting).
Verified: 2026-10-13 (tester, S5-V fourth sitting @ hb-20261013-01; production, reads only) — on a real plan (25 calls, 161 s; the tenant answering slowly, three `totals` calls split): `token {expiresInSeconds 3220, fits true, afterPullSeconds 3029, withProposals {seconds 161, fits true}}` with `kb.refreshSeconds` 0 and `templates {planned 0, seconds 0, secondsEach 3}`: `withProposals.seconds` = 161 + 0 + 0 and `afterPullSeconds` = 3220 − 161 − the margin. This tenant's knowledge base has no program or template gap today, so neither ask fires and no gap-fill starts (the bar's second clause, trivially); the asks' wording stays judged by the suite — a live walk of them needs a KB gap. VERIFIED on what the tenant can measure.

## F-510 — WONTFIX
Reported: 2026-10-10 (tester, V2 first sitting @ hb-20261010-01 on dev; production tenant, reads only; VALIDATION Y2)
Severity: polish — proposed WONTFIX under R1 ruling 5 (2026-10-05: a category cuts what the email rule misses); the text sits in the run directory's sample payload files only, in the workspace, and none of it reached the snapshot
What: the fetch-time mask leaves an address intact when the mail service wrote its domain with a stray space before the top-level domain (the email rule needs `@label.label`), and the same local part appears once more as a bare word before the parenthesis; a directory service's "user not listed" wording carries that shape. In 3148 sample messages across 50 payload files: 5 such messages (2 more `@` hits are a bare `@domain` with no local part). Y2's payload clause reads zero `@` hits, so it FAILED on these 5; the snapshot's 2740 health texts read 0 (the 5 were not among the per-program top-five distinct texts).
Repro: a `--health` pull on a tenant whose bounces include that wording; search the `health-bounce-sample` payload files' `message` fields for `@`.
Expected: WONTFIX on the ruling, with the ruled remedy applied: the wording's invariant core goes into the tenant's `--failure-categories` file (its tail is cut at the next pull), which Bradley rules on at V2.5; or, if he wants the mask to catch it, the email rule allows one space inside the domain when a top-level domain follows, pinned by a fixture row of this shape.
Ruling: 2026-10-11 (Bradley, at V2's second sitting @ hb-20261010-01) — WONTFIX under R1 ruling 5; remedy applied: a "not listed in directory" bounce category appended to the tenant's workspace category file (validated), so from the next health pull the wording is counted under it and the sample's exclusion filter never fetches those rows. The residue (the mask misses a domain written with a space on any other tenant until its admin adds the category) is a known issue in the plan's backlog (LTR-18), not a reopen trigger.

Expected: the fast path applies each question's labelled default through the same `apply` the interview uses (one source for a default, never two); for grouping it writes the characteristic rules the proposal would lead with (recurring / one-off at the top level, model beneath) so the standard dashboard is grouped; the note names the real slug; a test holds the fast-path spec equal to answering every question with its default.
