## F-513 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-12 (tester)
Severity: normal — a dashboard with customer lists and Health on a tenant this size can never be pulled, and the saved dashboard has no pages
What: Class, in one sentence: the refresh budget gate holds the WHOLE pull to the login remaining seconds, so a first pull longer than one login maximum (60 minutes) can never start, and its remedy (log in, run refresh again, it resumes) loops with nothing to resume, while the adapter underneath is built to stop on expiry and resume.
Repro: S5-V second sitting @ hb-20261012-01, production, reads only: dashboard new <x> with the customer lists, Health and step detail on a tenant whose plan prices the full pull above one login (191 programs, 13 months, 2 internal domains, 2 test accounts: 763 calls, 4327 s); answer save yes on a FRESH login: exit 3, "the dashboard is saved; its first refresh stopped: the refresh needs about 73 minutes (763 calls plus re-documentation) and the login has 60 minutes left - run the login, then run refresh again (it resumes)". Log in and run refresh <x>: the same refusal, nothing made, nothing to resume. The gate (dashboard.mjs refresh: needed = thisRun.seconds + redoc + 30 > whoami expiresInSeconds) runs before the first fact call.
Expected: Bradley's ruling (2026-10-12, in session): the pull must CHECKPOINT across logins. A pull longer than the login runs as far as the token allows, stops cleanly with exit 3 keeping the calls made (the adapter already does this mid-pull: engagement.mjs stops when the next call would outlast the token and resumes), and the next run after a login continues it; the gate refuses only what cannot progress at all (no valid token), and the message says how many logins a first pull of this size will take. README section Scheduled already promises this ("the first pull is full and may need more than one login ... the next run resumes it"); the gate contradicts it.
Note: 2026-10-12 (tester, the same sitting, R8) — two more measurements for the class. (1) Every login is a browser flow the admin completes by hand (Bradley: "I still have to manually go through the authentication"), so a scheduled run can never log itself in: the checkpoint is the only shape that works for a pull longer than one login, and the message's "how many logins" is what the admin plans around. (2) Even a SELECTIVE refresh of this dashboard (lists off; Health with two internal domains and two test accounts: 6 recipient classes × 56 categories) is longer than one login on this tenant: R8's first firing ran 18:05 to 18:56:55, 423 calls, and stopped on the expired token (exit 3, the pages untouched); the resumed firing after a login finished it. The gate let it start because its estimate priced the run inside the hour; the adapter's own stop-and-resume carried it. The gate protects nothing the adapter does not already handle.
Fix: 2026-10-12 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-fix2 merged into feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261012-02; Bradley's ruling and the Note applied) — Class, in one sentence: the refresh held the WHOLE pull to one login where the adapter underneath already checkpoints call by call. The budget gate is gone. The refresh plans, says on stderr when the pull will take more than one login ("it will run as far as the login allows (about N logins of an hour in all) and continue after the next login"), re-documents, and pulls; the adapter stops cleanly when the next call would outlast the token (as it did mid-pull) and the stop's message says how many calls this run made (and reused), "run gs-admin login, then run refresh <slug> again: it continues where it stopped", and about how many more logins of an hour the pull needs (none left: "every call is made: the next run finishes it"); a login that dies under the re-documentation step is the same stop (exit 3, resumable), not a failure. The summary carries `budget {neededSeconds, loginSecondsLeft, fitsThisLogin, loginsNeeded}`. One rule for the arithmetic: `LOGIN_SECONDS` (3600, the hour-long login the auth doc records) and `loginsFor(seconds)`; the closing step's login clause ("your login has about T minutes left, so the first refresh will take about N logins of an hour: it runs as far as each login allows, stops, and continues when you log in and run it again"), the estimate's confirmation (`loginsNeeded`), the `change` verb's pull pricing ("about N logins of an hour" past one) and the README (a pull longer than one login is not refused; every login is a browser flow completed by hand, so a schedule is a reminder with the run attached) say the same. What the Note measured is now the only shape: the gate refused only what the adapter would have carried.
Judge: the entry-command suite's F-513 walk: a refresh on a login of 60 seconds against a pull of hundreds of seconds is NOT refused (stderr names the logins), the stand-in CLI kills the token after thirty calls, the refresh stops with exit 3 after the calls it made, its message names the login to run, that the next run continues, and about how many more logins, the stale lock it took over is recorded in that refusal, the run stays resumable and no snapshot is written; the next `refresh` resumes it (`resumed: true`, calls reused) to a completed pull; `loginsFor` pinned at the hour boundary; the closing ask's two-login case and the estimate's `loginsNeeded` pinned over the fixture plan.
Verified: 2026-10-13 (tester, S5-V third sitting @ hb-20261012-02; production, reads only; Bradley's by-hand logins) — I10 on a pull priced above one login (763 calls, 4327 s): "Save and run the first refresh now" was NOT refused; stderr at the start: "needs about 73 minutes and the login has 25 minutes left: it will run as far as the login allows (about 2 logins of an hour in all) and continue after the next login"; the estimate's confirmation read the token then (loginsNeeded 2). The pull stopped exit 3 after 111 calls (19 reused from the closing step's plan) with the message as the bar ("run gs-admin login, then run refresh <dash> again: it continues where it stopped; the last good pages are untouched — about 1 more login of an hour to finish"); `status` showed the resumable run, no pages, no snapshot, no lock. After the F-512 change and a second stop on the expired login (294 calls), the resume after a login ran to exit 0 (313 calls reused), the snapshot written and both pages built. The scheduled firing without a login (I15): exit 3, status token-expired, pages untouched. Wall against estimate: the fresh pull about 85 minutes against 67 estimated, about 8 calls a minute against the plan's 10. Observation recorded as F-518 on Bradley's call: the resume's opening line and its `budget` priced the WHOLE plan (67 minutes, 2 logins) although 313 calls were reused and the remainder fit the login. The stop that is NOT the login's — a call the adapter gave up on — is F-519's, a different mechanism.

## F-514 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-12 (tester, S5-V second sitting @ hb-20261012-01 on feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command; VALIDATION § DSH-3 I1; no tenant call)

Every other question has two to four options (window 4, look 3, customer-list-detail 3, the closing step 4).

Expected: Bradley's ruling owed (the six options are his ruling 4): either the options fold to four (the three day spans as one option with a follow-up for the span, say) or the skill prose says how a question with more than four options is asked (the first four, then a second ask for the rest, never "Other"); a test holds every option list to the tool's limit or to the prose's rule.

A question with more than four options is asked in chat as a NUMBERED LIST (the ask, then the options verbatim, numbered), the admin replies with the number or the option's words, the follow-ups run as usual, never "Other" or a "more choices" entry; the question tool stays for every question that fits its four. Ruling 4's six options stand unchanged.
Fix: 2026-10-12 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-fix2 merged into feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261012-02) — Class, in one sentence: an option list was not held to what the asking tool can show, and the prose had no rule for the overflow. The skill's D3 carries the rule as ruled: a question with more than four options is asked in chat as a numbered list of the `options`' `text` verbatim in the script's order, ending "Reply with the number."; the reply is matched to one option (a number, or the option's own words) and the flow continues, follow-ups included; a reply matching none is asked again; never "Other", never a "more choices" entry, never an option left out. The table is unchanged (the programs question keeps its six).
Judge: the entry-command suite holds every non-judgment question's option list to four except the programs question's six (the one list the rule covers today), and holds the skill's prose to the rule's three parts (more than four options, a numbered list, never "Other"); the script's own refusal of an answer outside its options (pinned since S5) bounds a mis-read reply.
Verified: 2026-10-13 (tester, S5-V third sitting @ hb-20261012-02; no tenant call beyond the interview's own) — the programs question asked in chat as a numbered list of its six options verbatim in the script's order, ending "Reply with the number."; Bradley replied "3", matched to the third option and its follow-up; no "Other", no "more choices" entry; every other question asked through the question tool with its two to four options.

## F-516 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-12 (tester, S5-V second sitting @ hb-20261012-01 on feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command; VALIDATION § DSH-3 I8 on an edit, § UX-2 B1–B4; production tenant, reads only)
Severity: normal — an admin who edits a saved dashboard through the skill is asked the whole interview again, and the closing step never comes after a dry run on an edit
What: Class, in one sentence: an edit over a saved dashboard starts with nothing marked answered, so `next` walks the interview from the first question instead of from the saved answers. Measured: `new <x>` over the saved dashboard (state `editing-saved`) returned `answered: []`, `next: programs`; after `next --question look` (the go-back path, `again: true`), `answer look <json>` and `answer dry-run yes` (the themed preview written), `next` returned the programs question with `progress {answered 3, remaining 15}` — the three being the tenant, the look and the dry run — so the skill's D3 ("never skip one it returned") would re-ask the 15 saved settings, and I8's "the closing step is then asked again without the dry-run option" cannot happen on an edit. Repro: on a saved dashboard: `dashboard.mjs new <x> --kb <kb>` then `next <x>`: the programs question, not the closing step; `answer <x> dry-run yes` then `next`: the programs question again.
Expected: an edit's draft marks every setting the saved spec holds as answered (ask-once from the saved spec), so `next` on an edit goes to the closing step, which states "rebuild" or "new pull" from what the draft changed (the 2026-10-04 ruling: `dashboard edit` is draft-then-save and `save` states the consequence first), and `next --question <id>` is the one way to change a setting; the skill's D2 says this for `dashboard edit`; a test holds `new` over a saved spec followed by `next` to the closing step with nothing re-asked.
Fix: 2026-10-12 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-fix2 merged into feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261012-02) — Class, in one sentence: an edit's draft was a copy of the saved spec with nothing marked answered, so the interview could not tell it from a new dashboard. `new` over a saved spec marks every setting question answered (the saved spec holds them), so `next` goes straight to the closing step; the interview context carries `edit {changed, consequence}` from the same `changeCost(saved, draft)` the `change` verb reads, and the closing ask states what the edit changes against the saved dashboard and what it costs ("the next refresh pulls everything again, about M minutes" / "the customer lists are ranked again … no pull" / "the pages are rebuilt … no pull" / "Nothing changed against the saved dashboard"); its options are the consequence's (save and run the refresh / rebuild the pages / rank the lists again now; a preview; save only or "Close the edit (nothing changed)"; go back), no plan is made for an edit that needs no pull, and `save yes` DOES the consequence through the one `doConsequence` the `change` verb uses. `next --question <id>` is the way to change one setting (the summary's hint lists the ids), after which the closing step restates the consequence. An edit's dry run previews the draft's settings over the LAST PULL with no call (the option reads "Preview the pages first (rebuilt from the last pull with these settings; no call)"), so the themed preview UX-2 promises costs no login minutes; a `--fast-path` given on an edit is said to be ignored, never dropped in silence. The skill's D2 describes the edit flow and D3's closing step the options' edit forms.

## F-519 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-13 (tester, S5-V third sitting @ hb-20261012-02 on feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command; production, reads only; VALIDATION § DSH-3 I15, the scheduled task's firings; the run's status.json and fetch-log in the workspace's engagement run directory are the evidence)
Severity: normal — a saved dashboard whose refresh meets one slow response on an unsplittable call can never be refreshed again by any verb the skill or the pages name; the remedy the message gives loops; the only exit is a hand-removed state file
What: Class, in one sentence: a call the adapter gave up on is replayed as final on every resume, so a transient failure becomes a permanent one for the life of the run. Measured: the scheduled firing's selective refresh (172 calls, 36 minutes) had ONE call — the participants family for one program over the window — time out twice (45 s and 51 s); that family has no smaller unit (`timeoutSplit` false), so `runUnit` recorded "nothing left to split on", and the run ended `partial` (exit 4; status.json `failed: [{family resp-participants, kind timeout}]`; the other 171 calls done; the pages untouched; the run resumable) with the message "the refresh stopped after 172 calls this run (18 reused from before): partial —  run refresh <dash> again: it continues where it stopped; the last good pages are untouched" (an empty slot before "run": `r.summary.stopped` is unset for a partial, and the message names neither the call nor the cause). The next firing after a fresh login made ONE call (whoami) and stopped identically ("after 1 call this run (188 reused from before): partial"): `runUnit` reuses a prior record whose status is `split` (`prior.status === "split"` counts as reused and is never re-executed), then finds no split and records the same failure. The same call had answered in one attempt (171 rows, about 9 s) in the first full pull the night before. `refresh --full` would be refused as a flag change ("is waiting to resume: run it again with the same flags, or remove …/refresh-state.json to start over"), so the state file's removal by hand is the only exit, and only that refusal names it (the remedy class F-512's reopen named). On a monthly schedule every firing fails into the log within seconds, for ever; the admin's page keeps saying "run the same command again". Not a testing artifact: the task ran the README's refresh line as printed, and the timeout was the server's.
Repro: a saved dashboard with a pending run whose fetch-log carries a row `{"status":"split","kind":"timeout"}` for a family with `timeoutSplit: false` (or: stop a refresh after a participants call has timed out twice); run `refresh <dash> --kb <folder>` after a login: one call, exit 4, the same `failed` entry; run it again: the same.
Expected: a resume RE-RUNS a row that did not succeed (a `split` or `failed` row is a fresh attempt on the next run, never reused; a timeout that recurs across N runs may then be reported as a failure of record with the program counted), so a transient timeout on an unsplittable call costs one more firing, not the dashboard; the partial stop's message says what failed (the family, one program, "a server timeout"), that the next run retries it, and has no empty slot; a test holds a run stopped on an unsplittable timeout, resumed with the stand-in answering, to a completed pull with `calls.retried` above 0.
Fix: 2026-10-13 (builder, feat/jo-dash-s5-fix3 merged into feat/jo-dash-s5-entry-command, PR #47 unmerged, hb-20261013-01) — Class, in one sentence: the adapter's resume treated every prior record as a settled answer, so a record that recorded a failed attempt ("split" on a unit with nothing left to cut, which it is for the whole survey family and the per-program samples) was replayed as the outcome of every later run. Root cause, in `runUnit`: `prior.status === "split"` counted as reused; for a splittable unit that is the right reading (the decision to cut stands and the halves carry the attempts), for an unsplittable one it was the failure itself. Now a prior "split" record is reused only when the unit CAN be cut (`cutsOf`, the one rule `runUnit` and the plan's remainder share), a failed record is never reused, and the resume makes the call afresh through `execute`, which carries `runs` (the runs a call has failed in) onto the record and the failure entry, so a timeout that recurs run after run is reported as recurring rather than new each time; every failure entry names the programs the unit covered when it named any. The stop's message in the entry command reads the failed list (`failedText`): "1 call failed: resp-participants timed out on the server twice (a server timeout)[ in N runs so far] — run refresh <slug> again: it retries what failed and continues where it stopped; the last good pages are untouched" — no empty slot (the "run gs-admin login, then" prefix is built with its own space). Sibling the tester did not list, run against the fix: a `failed` record from a shape error or an unparseable answer (never reused before either, so the same path: made afresh, `runs` counted); and a prior "split" record on a SPLITTABLE family stays a reused decision (the engagement suite's "timed out twice: split" check unchanged). The skill's exit-4 prose (report mode, the pull-again mode, the dashboard verbs) says the error names the call and that the next run retries it; the README's refresh paragraph says the same. The tester's evidence (the run directory's status.json: `failed: [{resp-participants, timeout}]`, `calls {made 1, reused 188}`; the fetch-log's one `"status":"split","kind":"timeout","attempt":2` row; the log's two "partial —  run refresh" lines) was read in the workspace, never copied.
Judge: the entry-command suite drives the stand-in CLI (its fault counter persists across invocations) to time the survey participants count out three times in a row: the first run stops partial (exit 4) with the message above, no empty slot, the status entry carrying `runs: 1`, no snapshot; the second run RE-MAKES the call (two more `rp run` lines on that family in the stand-in's argv log), its retry answers (`calls.retried` above 0), and it completes with exit 0, a snapshot and no state file; a four-fault variant then shows the second partial stop saying "in 2 runs so far" with the status entry at `runs: 2`, and a later run completing it. The tester's live arm (I15's resume on the real dashboard, § DSH-3 fourth sitting) is the judge of record.
Verified: 2026-10-13 (tester, S5-V fourth sitting @ hb-20261013-01; the branch at 008d1d1, clean and level; production, reads only; the scheduled task recreated from the README's Windows recipe for the firing pair, then deleted) — the FALLBACK path, recorded as the bar allows: no unsplittable call timed out on the server this sitting (firing 1, a selective refresh of 524 planned calls, stopped on the login's expiry after 61 calls, exit 3, `failed: []`; its one timeout, a `totals` call, was split and answered). The pending run's fetch-log was given ONE `split`/`timeout` row (`attempt` 2, `runs` 1, the third sitting's evidence shape) for a `uniques-window` unit the run had answered — a unit the adapter's own `splitUnit` returns null for; no state file touched. Firing 2 after a login RE-MADE that call as its fourth line ("pull uniques-window-… ok (21024 ms)"; a third row for the id, `ok`, after the split row; `calls.made` counting it) and ran on to the login's expiry (494 made, 81 reused, 61 split, 1 retried, `failed: []`, the stop saying "every call is made: the next run finishes it"); firing 3 after a login finished it: exit 0, `resumed: true`, 31 made / 572 reused, a new snapshot, both pages moved, the state file and the lock gone, the task's Last Result 0. Never a stop within seconds with `calls.made: 1`. The partial stop's message (`failedText`, "retries what failed", no empty slot) and the status entry's `runs: 1` stay measured on the stand-in only: no run ended partial here. The third sitting's stuck run directory and the refresh log removed at cleanup, as agreed.

## F-520 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-13 (tester, S6-V @ hb-20261013-02 on feat/jo-dash-s6-account-timeline at 1c2754e; production, reads only; VALIDATION § ACC A2)
Severity: normal — the timeline page and the summary tell the admin the dashboard did not keep this account on a program when it did; no figure is wrong, the stated reason is
What: Class, in one sentence: the dashboard comparison decides which programs "kept" the account from the account's rows inside the months it COMPARES (the whole months the timeline covers), so a program whose timeline sends fall only outside those months — the partial first month of the window, or the provisional current month — is reported as one the dashboard did not keep. Measured: account 2 of the round, through the dashboard's own copy line, `against.compared` 11 and `matches-dashboard` ok (11 of 11 closed-month cells equal, confirmed by an independent recount from the two files and by three direct counts of one program-month: sent, delivered and opened equal); `notCompared` named 3 programs with `account-not-kept-on-program`, and the dashboard's latest snapshot holds the account's own rows on all 3 (one carried over ten months, one carried in the window's first month, one pulled in the current month). Their timeline days fall only in the window's first, partial month (two) or in the provisional month (one). The page's About renders it as "3 programs not compared (the dashboard did not keep this account there)". Code: `reconcileWithDashboard` (engagement.mjs, the `kept` set from `runQuery(snapshot, {months, accounts, accountBuckets: ["account"]}, …)` with `months` = the compared months); the sibling: the `!kept.size` branch below it gives the same reason for an account whose timeline has no send in a compared month although the dashboard holds its rows.
Repro: a dashboard pulled with customer lists on; an account it kept that has, inside the timeline's days, sends on some program ONLY in the window's partial first month or in the current month; `dashboard.mjs account <dash> --account-id <GSID> --kb <folder>`: read `against.notCompared[].reason` and the page's About line "Against the dashboard" against the snapshot's `facts.byAccount` rows of that account and program.
Expected: a program is "not kept" only when the dashboard holds no row of the account on it at all (over the snapshot's window); a program it holds but whose timeline sends fall outside the compared months is named apart, with its own reason ("no send in the months compared", or whatever wording the builder chooses), and the page sentence says that; the same for the whole-account branch.

## F-521 — VERIFIED

Code: `selectionFor` (engagement.mjs: the `across` map skips every carried program; `previousSelection` is consulted for the per-program sets only).

Expected: a selective refresh keeps lists the admin can read: either the previous snapshot's lists carry forward with the carried programs (and the record says so), or the lists are re-ranked over the embedded rows the snapshot holds; never an empty list stated as "no account met this list's floor" while the accounts are in the snapshot. A test holds a selective refresh's list record to the full refresh's over unchanged data.
Fix: 2026-10-13 (builder) — (feat/jo-dash-s6-fix merged into feat/jo-dash-s6-account-timeline, PR #48 unmerged, hb-20261013-03) — Class, in one sentence: a selective refresh holds whole-window figures only for the accounts already kept, so the ranking it made over the programs pulled whole was a ranking of nothing when every program is carried, and never the full pull's when some are. The builder's design call, CARRY, not re-rank, and why: every other account's carried months sit in the "all other accounts" row, so no ranking a selective refresh can make is the one a full pull makes; a re-rank among the kept would present a partial ranking as a whole one, where carrying the last full ranking is exact over unchanged data and says what it is. `carriedLists` (engagement.mjs): a selective refresh carries the previous snapshot's lists as ranked, per-segment ones included; each list record gains `rankedAt` (the full pull that ranked it), `carriedFrom` (the snapshot carried from; null on a full pull) and `notRanked` (null, or why there was no ranking to carry: `list-set-since`, read from the previous pull's own params echo, for a list configured after it — a list change is a rebuild, never a pull, ruled 2026-10-05 — and `previous-not-ranked` for a record ranked over part of the programs, the code before this fix; then `kept` is empty and `selectedFrom` null). The accounts the cross-program lists keep get their own rows on every program they are on, carried programs included (before, only the programs pulled whole), so their figures stay whole along a chain of refreshes. The report: "These lists were ranked by the full pull of <date> …" above carried lists; a not-ranked list says so with the engine's sentence and that a full refresh (`refresh <slug> --full`) ranks it; "No account met this list's floor" only for a list ranked and empty (with "at the full pull of <date>" when carried). T-10 additive: three fields on each list record, documented at the record; the fixture snapshot regenerated (those fields only). For the re-check: v2's latest snapshot is the pre-fix selective one (lists recorded empty), so a selective refresh straight from it reads "not ranked" — the arm starts with a full refresh. Siblings run against the fix: a list set since the full pull among three carried (not ranked, the others carried); a per-segment list set at the full pull with no segment then (carried as none, never "set since": the review's finding). Pick up: /reload-plugins.
Judge: the engagement suite: a selective refresh over unchanged fixture data records the full refresh's lists exactly (kind, n, floor, per, segment, kept, in order) with `rankedAt` and `carriedFrom` the full pull's, the account table's totals equal, and `buildReport` prints the lists with no floor-miss line and the same count of cross-program lists (3); a pre-fix record and a list set since each read not ranked with the engine's sentence in the report. ## F-529 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-14 (builder, R12 release-gate review: /code-review medium over origin/main..dev scoped to the plugin's scripts, skills and hooks; finder + opus verifier, reproduced with the stand-in CLI)
Severity: normal — a decision is made wrong: `change` reports the customer lists ranked when they are not, and names a no-pull remedy that does not rank them
Class: outcome-from-proxy
What: Class, in one sentence: a reselect reports the lists re-ranked because the reduce ran, not because a list was ranked. dashboard.mjs reselectFromRun re-reduces the latest run with that run's own previous snapshot; decideRefresh leaves `lists` out of the account-selection comparison (engagement.mjs selectionFor / carriedLists), so over a SELECTIVE latest pull (every refresh after the first) a new or resized list is written `keys: []`, `notRanked: "list-set-since"`, while `change` exits 0 with `done: true` and "the customer lists are ranked again over the last pull's rows"; the next selective refresh marks it previous-not-ranked, and only an unpriced `refresh --full` ranks it. Instances on the same mechanism: (2) with the run directory gone (import --snapshot, tmp cleaned) reselect returns done:false before buildPages, so the other changed settings in the same `change` (title, groups, publish) are saved but the pages are not rebuilt; (3) the same day as the first save, with Health off, an edit that reaches a plan question resumes the pulled plan directory and rewrites its status.json to phase plan, and the next reselect dies on loadRun's uncaught "not complete" with a stack trace.
Repro: stand-in workspace (test/dashboard.mjs's first ~388 lines): save, first refresh, a plain `refresh` (selective), then `change <dash> accounts.lists=[{"kind":"most-bounced","n":3,"floor":0}]`: exit 0, done true; the snapshot's list has kept 0, notRanked list-set-since. The suite tests reselect only on a full first snapshot (test/dashboard.mjs ~421).
Expected: a list change ranks the lists it promises or says plainly that a full pull is needed and prices it; done reflects what was ranked; a reselect that cannot run rebuilds the other changes; no uncaught error on a run directory in plan phase.
Routing: the R12 fix round, before the recut.
Ruling: 2026-10-15 (Bradley, R12 release gate, after the cross-round read: F-521 settled that a ranking is made only at a full pull; the S5 reselect promise was never revisited) — split by scope. Fix round A ships the NARROW honest fix: when the latest pull was full, reselect re-ranks as today; when it was selective, `change` saves the list, re-ranks nothing, says plainly that the list is ranked at the next full refresh (`refresh <dash> --full`), and reports done truthfully; instance (2) (a reselect that cannot run) rebuilds the other changed settings; instance (3) (a run directory in plan phase) is a refusal, never a stack trace. The ROOT (a list re-ranked on every refresh) is F-548, DEFERRED past 0.54.0 to session B; when B lands, this narrow path is replaced.
Routing: R12 fix round A, before the 0.54.0 recut.
Fix: 2026-10-15 (builder) — (feat/r12-fix-a, PR #53, hb-20261015-01) — the NARROW fix as ruled. Class, in one sentence: a change reported the lists re-ranked because the reduce ran, not because a list was ranked; the outcome now comes from what the reduce can rank over. dashboard.mjs reselectReadiness decides it once, read by every reader: ranked now only when the latest snapshot's meta.refresh.mode is "full" AND its run directory (matched by the exact pulledAt among this dashboard's own runs, F-535) is a finished pull (status ok, phase all); otherwise reselectFromRun ranks nothing, rebuilds the pages from the latest snapshot so every other changed setting of the same change lands (instance 2), and returns done false, ranked false, rebuilt, why (a routine refresh; the rows gone; a run directory not a finished pull — instance 3 is now this refusal, never loadRun's stack), fullRefreshMinutes, remedy.line = `refresh <dash> --kb <kb> --full` and a one-sentence done.text. The same readiness words change's consequenceText (dry run included), the edit's closing ask and its first option ("Save and rebuild the pages now (no pull; the customer lists are ranked at the next full refresh)"), and COST_KINDS.reselect. Root-cause cost named: none here — the root (a list re-ranked on every refresh) is F-548, deferred to session B, and this narrow path is replaced when B lands. Pick up: /reload-plugins.

## F-531 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-10-14 (builder, R12 release-gate review, verifier reproduced over snapshot-acme with the current month scaled to day 2)
Severity: normal — every count tile on the admin page's default view shows a drop that did not happen early in a month
What: Class, in one sentence: the headline tiles' change divides a sum that includes the provisional month by a month count that includes it, against a usual measured over closed months only. engagement-query.mjs: change = value / months / usual where months = scope.months.length; the admin preset's dateDefault "window" keeps the provisional month. On day 2 the fixture's Sent tile reads 0.76x the usual while every closed month equals it (about 0.92x over a 12-month window). The tile's * explains late opens, not the divisor. DSH-4 D0 ruled the usual (the window's finished months), not the numerator.
Repro: snapshot-acme with the current month's sends scaled to 2/30, the admin page's default view: Sent "0.76x the usual"; closed months only: 1.00.
Expected: the change compares like with like (closed months against closed months, or the partial month pro-rated and said), and the tile says which.
Routing: the R12 fix round, before the recut.
Routing: 2026-10-15 (Bradley, R12) — R12 fix round A, before the 0.54.0 recut.
Fix: 2026-10-15 (builder) — (feat/r12-fix-a, PR #53, hb-20261015-01) — Class, in one sentence: a change against the usual compared a sum that holds the provisional month, divided by a month count that counts it, with a usual over closed months only. engagement-query.mjs kpiView now computes the change over the CLOSED months the view keeps (the provisional month left out; a view with no closed month has no change) and returns change.months {closed, provisionalLeftOut}; the tile says it: "(over the N closed months shown; the current month is left out until it closes)", or "no closed month shown to compare with it". My call between the ruling's two (closed months, or the provisional month pro-rated and said): closed months — pro-rating a month whose opens are still arriving reads a drop the tile's * already warns about. Consequence for Bradley's eye (VALIDATION V2): in the default whole-window view the change now reads level, because the window's closed months ARE the usual. Siblings fixed the same way: a rate tile (points over the closed months), and the Health tab's bounce-reason Change column (healthReasonsView: the closed months of the period, changeMonths returned, the column says "(closed months)"). Golden page regenerated. Pick up: /reload-plugins; rebuild a dashboard to see it.

## F-466 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-09-26 (tester 1.0.10-V @ hb-20260926-01, hit while building its rig and not logged; reproduced and logged by the builder after PR #27 merged, on Bradley's call)
Severity: normal — the guard's pipe-safety lint first-offense-DENIES a legitimate command that runs no gs-admin at all, whenever the text "gs-admin" appears anywhere in it; reachable in any workspace whose paths or arguments carry the word (this repo's own name does). Not high: the repeat escalates to an ask, and no mutation ask is removed or downgraded
Class: second-scanner
What: hooks/gs-admin-guard.mjs gates on the RAW text — `if (!/gs-admin/i.test(command)) process.exit(0);` (~:316) — and past that gate the pipe-safety lint (findSuspiciousMeta over the whole command's words) inspects EVERY unquoted `|` / lone `&` in the command, whether or not a gs-admin invocation feeds that pipeline. So `git -C <path containing gs-admin> archive HEAD | tar -x …` draws the coaching deny aimed at asset-name fragments ("`tar` would run as a command. Gainsight asset names …"), although no gs-admin runs. Class candidate, to confirm at fix time: second-scanner — the lint's SCOPE is decided from the raw text, not from the tokenizer's record of which segments a gs-admin invocation occupies.
Repro: drive the hook in place per AGENTS.md's recipe (spawnSync, cwd inside a throwaway dir holding `.gs-superadmin/`, hook_event_name PreToolUse, tool_name Bash), measured 2026-09-26 on dev:
    P1 git -C /work/gs-admin-cli-docs archive HEAD | tar -x -C /work/out  → deny (coaching: `tar` would run as a command)
    P2 git -C /work/other-repo archive HEAD | tar -x -C /work/out         → pass-through (control)
    P3 echo hi | tar -x                                                   → pass-through (control)
    P4 ls gs-admin | tar -x                                               → deny
    P5 ls /opt/tools/gs-admin | tar -x                                    → deny
    P6 gs-admin --json jo p list | tar -x                                 → deny (the lint's intended target)
Expected: the lint applies only to a pipeline a gs-admin invocation participates in, decided from the tokenizer's record (the invocation's segment and the operator that follows it), never from the raw text — P1, P4, P5 pass through, P6 is still coached. Tenets 1-3 hold by construction: the change can only remove a coaching deny on a command that runs no gs-admin; it never touches a mutation ask. Pin P1/P4/P5/P6 in test/guard-fixtures.mjs and add non-gs-admin pipelines to the shell-oracle generator (test/guard-oracle.mjs) so the scope is judged against the real shell, not a list. Gates the next release unless fixed or deliberately deferred.
Defer: 2026-09-26 (Bradley) - past 0.43.0. Why not now: shipped unchanged in every release of this repo — the raw-text gate and the lint's whole-command scope date from its first commit (2026-09-09, seeded from the private predecessor); the effect is a first-offense coaching deny on a command that runs no gs-admin, which a retry turns into an ask, and no mutation ask is lost or downgraded; the fix is a guard round (fixtures plus the shell oracle), while 0.43.0 carries the README beginner path the community post is gated on. Fix: 2026-09-28 (builder, branch fix-f461-f466). Class confirmed: second-scanner — the lint's SCOPE came from the raw text (the command-text gate let a line through, and the lint then judged every operator on it). hooks/gs-admin-guard.mjs now takes the scope from the scan's own reading. scanWords gains an optional `named` set, passed only by the top-level balanced pass, and records the name index of every invocation the lint may judge: any at command position, and at operand position only one whose words match a catalog command (the wrapper spelling: `npx gs-admin …`, the capture helper's `-- gs-admin …`); a bare name (`ls gs-admin`) never qualifies. The lint's execution moved below the scan (its helpers stay where they were; a first offense still denies before anything is reported), and findSuspiciousMeta judges an operator only when the chain of segments that `|`, `|&` and a lone `&` join, walked left from it, holds one of those invocations. A span (`$(…)`, a subshell, a group) is one word of its segment; `;`, `&&`, `||` and a newline end the chain. The scan's asks are untouched. P1 now passes through. P4 and P5 no longer draw the lint and get the scan's existing fail-closed operand ask instead (F-436, the `which gs-admin` rule): the Expected's "pass through" for them would have removed an ask, which tenet 3 forbids, so the fix stops at the lint. P6 is still coached. Sibling found by the existing battery: `echo 'gs-admin jo p save' | bash` drew the lint's deny in a default workspace (its F-436 fixture pinned the deny); it now draws the mutating ask from the payload re-scan, the reading the consumer-list workspace already got — the F-443 shape, a false deny standing in for the right reading. Accepted boundary, pinned: an unquoted catalog call spelled as another command's arguments (`echo gs-admin jo p list | tar -x`) stays in scope, because it reads exactly like a wrapper; the scan asks on it for the same reason (F-051). A heredoc exclusion in the first draft was dropped: a body's words follow every operator on the opener's line and the chain walk only looks left, so removing it changed no decision (probed on bash heredocs and both PowerShell here-string quotes). Tests: test/guard-fixtures.mjs gains 20 F-466 pins (P1, P2, P4, P5, P6; the chain across a consumer-named fragment and across a lone `&`; the four list separators; a span each way; npx and the capture helper; a path ending in the name with non-catalog words; heredoc data; the accepted boundary) and re-pins the payload fixture above. test/guard-oracle.mjs gains the `mustNotLint` invariant, 59 generated no-run rows (9 positions of the text × `|`, `|&`, lone `&` × two right-hand programs the lint does not accept, glued `|`, heredoc data), and a run-wide count of lint denies on a line that ran no gs-admin. unpinned install now gets a CLI whose engines field says Node 20 or later. The error is
conservative (nothing breaks, nothing is silently wrong) and the current text is still
right for users on 1.0.9 - so the repair is version-conditional, never a replacement.

## F-464 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-09-26 (tester 1.0.10-V @ hb-20260926-01, observed beside F-463's pass bar and not logged; logged by the builder after PR #27 merged, on Bradley's call)
Severity: polish — the setup walk decided correctly on the `Token:` line; the skill's wording only leaves that to the agent's reading
What: setup SKILL.md Phase 1 says "Run `gs-admin whoami` to confirm authentication. If it fails (auth error or no tenant)…". On 1.0.10 `whoami` never fails: dist/commands/whoami.js logs every state and exits 0 — `Token: valid (expires in Ns)`, `Token: expired`, or `Token: none — run 'gs-admin login'`, beside `Base URL: … | (not set)`. On the enrollment path (no client credentials stored — the default) it also prints `Auth mode: not configured — run 'gs-admin login' (credentials auto-discovered)` while the token is valid, a line that reads like a failure and is not one. The branch is therefore decided by the agent's reading of the output, not by the words the skill uses.
Repro: after a normal `gs-admin login` on 1.0.10, run `gs-admin whoami; echo "exit=$?"` — exit 0, `Token: valid (…)`, and the `Auth mode: not configured — run 'gs-admin login' …` line; after expiry the same command still exits 0 with `Token: expired`. Read setup Phase 1's two paragraphs beside that output.
Expected: Phase 1 decides on named lines — `Token: valid` continues; `Token: expired` / `Token: none` stop with the re-login message; `Base URL: (not set)` gives the `--base-url` form (already named since 0.43.0) — and says the enrollment path's `Auth mode: not configured` line is not an auth failure. A SKILL.md change owes a walk (bus header walk hint), so this rides the next substantive round.
Fix: 2026-09-26 (builder, branch release-gate-0-43-0 — added to the 0.43.0 release-gate round by Bradley). setup SKILL.md Phase 1 now decides on the lines `whoami` prints, in order, never on its exit code (1.0.10's dist/commands/whoami.js, byte-identical to 1.0.9's, logs every state and returns — no error path): `Base URL: (not set)` → the `--base-url` login message; `Token: valid (…)` (or `Token: SID cookie set via env`) → continue; anything else — `Token: expired`, `Token: none — …`, or `whoami` itself erroring → the bare login message. It names the default auto-enrollment setup's `Auth mode: not configured — run 'gs-admin login'` line as normal, not an auth failure. Sibling, same class, fixed: the operating model's "If `whoami` fails → auth error" line now reads the `Token:` line and names the Auth mode line. Carried, not fixed: change-request SKILL.md's offline-mode sentence ("if `gs-admin whoami` fails (no CLI or no auth)") — the same class, but a change-request edit owes a change-request walk, the cost Bradley kept out of this round with F-461; it rides F-461's round. CHANGELOG 0.43.0 (unreleased) gains the line. Reload: /reload-plugins; the operating-model wording reaches a workspace through the scaffold refresh at the next setup or refresh run.
Judge: the tester's walk of setup Phase 1 on the live 1.0.10 CLI (slash-typed by Bradley) — the line it decided on and what it did — not this note's reading of whoami.js.
Sibling sweep: batched — polish; the class grep (`whoami` followed by fail / error / exit, over skills/, templates/, reference/ and the READMEs) found three sites: setup Phase 1 (fixed), the operating model's auth-error line (fixed), change-request's offline mode (carried, above).

Reported: 2026-09-26 (builder, the 0.43.0 release-gate review — /code-review medium over origin/main...dev)

What: the 1.0.10 adoption moved doc-lib's CLI_PIN_FACTS.cliVersion from "1.0.9" to "1.0.10", and pinFactsFor() applies the table only when the catalog in use carries exactly that version. The single-version stamp fits a plugin that supports one CLI; 0.43.0 supports two (the version-conditional token pre-flight exists for exactly that reason).
Repro: node plugins/gs-superadmin/scripts/domain-candidates.mjs diff over a manifest whose workspace .gs-superadmin/catalog.json carries meta.cliVersion "1.0.9" (otherwise the bundled catalog): pinFacts.applied false, notEnumerableBareCount 0, the four `re rules` per-asset reads (events, executions, s3-tasks, schedules) fall through to the indexing chain; under plugin 0.42.0 the same catalog applied the table.

Pinned in test/domain-candidates.mjs: a catalog at an earlier verified version applies the table; an unverified version does not.

The self-retirement comment states the rule for the list: an adoption that finds an entry changed drops the older versions. Prose that said "self-retiring at the next pin" moved in step (domain-candidates' header, setup's references/index-scope-notes.md). CHANGELOG 0.43.0 (unreleased) gains the line. test/domain-candidates.mjs: for each alsoVerifiedOn version, a workspace catalog at that version applies the table (four sublists bucketed, no not-applied warning, stamped still the pin) and an inert-record warning cites that version; the list's shape is pinned (x.y.z, distinct, not the stamp).

## F-448 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-09-09 (builder, at the 2026-09-09 docs-only cut)
Severity: normal — the release path is blocked for any cut that changes no plugin path; no user-facing behaviour is wrong, but a release cannot merge without weakening the gate
What: the main ruleset requires manifests and validate (ubuntu-latest | windows-latest | macos-latest), but validate-plugin.yml's pull_request trigger carried a paths filter. A release PR whose diff touches none of those paths (PR #7: CONTRIBUTING, README, .gitattributes, .github/*) never starts the workflow; an unstarted workflow reports no check run; GitHub shows the four contexts as "Expected" and the PR is BLOCKED with every reported check green. Every earlier release changed plugin bytes, so the gap never fired on the private predecessor.
Repro: open a PR to main from a release/* branch whose changed files are outside the paths list; gh pr checks lists only drift (full), guard, GitGuardian; gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus reads BLOCKED.
Tried and refuted at this cut: gh workflow run validate-plugin.yml --ref <release branch> -f full_matrix=true. All four jobs succeeded on the same head sha (run 34401015130), but GitHub's PR rollup counts only check suites raised by the PR's own events — the dispatch suite never appears in gh pr checks and the PR stayed BLOCKED. The bus header's "release-grade recheck" dispatch is evidence, never a gate.
Fix: 2026-09-09 (builder) — GitHub's documented shape for a required check behind a path filter (docs: "Handling skipped but required checks" — a workflow skipped by paths leaves its checks Pending; a job skipped by a job-level if reports Success). The pull_request trigger loses its paths filter; a new first job `changes` decides from the PR's own diff (git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD against the same pathspec list) and always answers run=true when the base is main or the event is not a pull_request; `validate` and `manifests` carry needs: changes + if: needs.changes.outputs.run == 'true'. Docs-only PRs to dev still start no runner for the battery (the jobs skip); PRs to main always run the full matrix. The push trigger keeps its paths filter (push events gate no merge, and not starting a run at all is F-266's point) — that list and the pathspec list in `changes` are the same fact in two homes, each commented to name the other. Cost of the root cause over a workaround: one CI-touching PR to dev and a recut of the release branch; the alternative (removing the four contexts from the ruleset for one merge) weakens the gate and leaves no trace in the repo.
Judge: the recut release PR's own required-check rollup — gh pr checks on the new head lists manifests and the three validate legs with the ruleset satisfied (mergeStateStatus not BLOCKED), or the fix is wrong; independent of anything the fixer asserts.
Judge fired 2026-09-09 (builder): PR #7 recut head 19349c9 — gh pr checks listed changes, manifests, validate (ubuntu-latest | windows-latest | macos-latest), drift (full), guard, all SUCCESS (validate-plugin run 34402673242); mergeStateStatus CLEAN; merged by Bradley as 756579e. Live arm on the fix PR itself (#8, run 34402234627): the changes job printed "run: plugin-affecting paths changed:" and validate (ubuntu-latest) + manifests ran rather than skipped. Verdict of record still owed by the other role. Sibling: docs-drift.yml carries no paths filter (it always runs), pr-target-guard is branch-filtered to PRs targeting main, where it is the only place it is required — no other required context sits behind a trigger-level filter.
Verdict: VERIFIED 2026-09-10 (Bradley, recorded by the builder session on his instruction). Pass bar: the four required contexts report on a PR to main from a branch that changes no plugin path, and a docs-only PR to dev starts no battery runner. Measured: (1) release PR #7 recut head 19349c9 — changes, manifests, validate (ubuntu-latest | windows-latest | macos-latest), drift (full), guard all SUCCESS (validate-plugin run 34402673242), mergeStateStatus CLEAN, merged 756579e; (2) fix PR #8 (run 34402234627) — the changes job printed "run: plugin-affecting paths changed:" and validate (ubuntu-latest) + manifests ran; (3) the skipped-path arm named on the hb-20260909-01 Blind spots line, measured on PR #15 (docs-only, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml): changes SUCCESS, validate SKIPPED, manifests SKIPPED, drift (full) pass, mergeStateStatus CLEAN. Blind spots: none — every arm the Fix note claims was exercised on a live PR.

## F-449 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-09-10 (tester — first live multi-tenant setup, a second tenant added to an existing workspace)
Severity: high — a wrong-answer surface in deps-report, which exists to answer "what breaks if I change object X"; buried assets return a confident "nothing depends on this"
Class: outcome-from-proxy
What: Phase 4's candidate gate measures overlap correctly and then permits a conclusion its own measurement refutes. On the sandbox tenant, `report list-objects` was excluded 2026-08-09 with this recorded reason:

    Redundant plus schema reference. 0 of 586 rows match by objectId, but 253 match by
    objectName against data-management, which indexes 591 objects keyed by name. The BI
    source-object schema surface is already covered there, and more completely.

253 of 586 is 43%. "More completely" appears to rest on 591 > 586, which says nothing about overlap. Result: roughly 333 MDA objects indexed nowhere on that tenant since 2026-08-09. The prod tenant hit the same shape this round (246 of 589) and correctly adopted the command as a `report-objects` domain of 589 assets — the same skill reaching opposite verdicts on near-identical evidence, which locates the defect in the decision rule, not the measurement.
A threshold pass over all 38 exclusions across both tenants found this is the only failure. Every other exclusion either accounts for 100% of rows (4 of 4, 3 of 3, 59 of 59), accounts for the remainder explicitly (3 of 6 indexed plus 3 named sentinel ids), or declares itself a judgment call (0 of 33 folders, "recorded not to be reopened").
Second half, same root: exclusions carry only `decidedAt` while blocks carry `recheckAfter`. The reversible decision gets a review date; the permanent one does not. The sandbox tenant's block `recheckAfter: 2026-09-09` also lapsed with nothing surfacing it.
Evidence basis — INFERRED, not re-measured: the refutation rests entirely on the two numbers written into the exclusion reason itself (253 matched of 586 rows, against a 591-object domain). The sandbox tenant's `report list-objects` was NOT re-run live this round, so "roughly 333 buried" is arithmetic on the record rather than a fresh count. A live re-run is the confirming measurement and has not happened.
Expected: an exclusion whose stated ground is "covered by another domain" cannot be recorded unless the recorded match count supports it — a rule binding the verdict to the number, not prose that cites one. And a permanent exclusion carries at least the review affordance a temporary block does.
Fix: 2026-09-11 (builder) — the rule moves out of Phase 4's prose and into the verb that records the decision. `manifest.mjs exclude` now takes exactly one of `--check <file>` (the JSON `domain-candidates.mjs check --out <file>` writes — its rows / uniqueIds / alreadyIndexed / matchedByDomain are copied into the ledger entry as `evidence`, never re-typed) or `--no-check "<why>"` (stored as `noCheck`, for a candidate no check can run: a payload with no items array, as `journey cta options`). The coverage claim is a FLAG, `--covered-by <domain>`, refused unless the check says every unique id is indexed under that one domain — and a check that says exactly that is refused WITHOUT the flag, so the verdict is bound in both directions; a partial check is refused outright; `--covered-by` with `--no-check` is refused. Exclusions take `--recheck-after` exactly as blocks do, and the diff flags a `recheckDue` exclusion by name with the same warning it already gives a lapsed block (refresh runs the diff and now relays both). The diff's `excluded` entries carry `kind` — coverage | judgment | legacy, derived from the RECORD, never from its prose — plus `coveredBy`, `evidence`, `noCheck`, `recheckAfter`, `recheckDue`. Existing entries are untouched and read `legacy`. Class named: the exclusion verdict was asserted from a proxy ("more completely", 591 > 586) instead of the measurement the same step had just taken. Contract: the GsExclusion typedef in manifest.mjs's header (T-2), pinned by contract-conformance. Prose: setup Phase 4 step 2 (the check fence gains `--out`) and step 3 (two fences, and the partial-overlap rule stated with this entry's own numbers), refresh's candidate relay. Version 0.38.0 (the verb's contract changes: a record write without evidence is refused). Pick up: /reload-plugins. Review round (medium, 8 finders): the check file was unbound from its candidate — `check --out` now requires `--command`, stamps it with `checkedAt`, and the verb refuses a file that measured another command; `--covered-by` uses the manifest's own domain grammar (it was narrower, making an underscore-named covering domain undecidable); the coverage rule is symmetric on "one domain holds every id" whether or not others overlap; the evidence flags are refused on `block` and `--remove`; `no-check` is its own kind so an unevidenced entry is never read as judgment; step 1's runtime-error exclusion and the 0-row sentence name their route.
Sibling sweep: the ADOPT direction is the sibling the tester did not list — `upsert-batch` of a NEW domain whose rows are all indexed elsewhere is not bound to the check either, and the sandbox holds a live instance: `journey data-designer list` is EXCLUDED on prod as covered by data-management (59 of 59 by name, recorded 2026-09-10) and ADOPTED on the sandbox as `journey-data-designer` (69 assets, 2026-07-10) whose 69 ids AND names all sit in the sandbox's own data-management — the same list, opposite verdicts, this entry's class. Not closed here: binding adoption to the check would touch every first-time index in Phase 3, which never runs a check. Recorded as evidence and put to Bradley for the verdict on which tenant decided correctly; the deciding question is whether `jo data-designer get` carries a dependency surface `dm objects describe` lacks. Re-reading both tenants' 38 existing exclusions through the new diff: all `legacy` (no evidence recorded); the live arm re-decides the sandbox's `report list-objects` through the new path and the other 37 are not re-litigated (the tester's threshold pass found each accounts for 100% or declares a judgment call).
Ruled: 2026-09-11 (Bradley; measured by the builder on the sandbox KB, same asset under both domains) — the journey rows are Data Designer output datasets, part of data management and listed under the journey namespace only because a program can use one as a participant source; the `jo data-designer get` payload (objectName, label, fieldCount, fields) is a strict subset of `dm objects describe` (which adds dbName, group, dataStore, schema, stats), and a dataset's lineage lives in its design (`data-designer` domain), never here. Prod's coverage exclusion was correct; the sandbox adoption is a duplicate view. Its re-decision through the verb's ACCEPT path is banked as the second dev/VALIDATION.md section and rides the same tester round, so the judge below gets both directions on real data. Carried to Session C2 as prose: index-scope-notes says which dm objects are Data Designer outputs is "not determinable from CLI data" — `jo data-designer list` IS that determination for the status it filters on.
Judge: (1) the fixture harness replays the live numbers through the real verb — 253 of 586 with --covered-by REFUSED quoting the numbers, 59 of 59 accepted ONLY as coverage, 3 + 3 split across two domains accepted only as judgment, partial and 0-row checks handled as the Expected demands (manifest-ops.mjs, domain-candidates.mjs, contract-conformance.mjs) — that is the fixer's own list; (2) independent of it, the tester's live arm on the sandbox, banked in dev/VALIDATION.md: lift the 2026-08-09 exclusion, capture `report list-objects` fresh, `check --out`, and the verb must refuse `--covered-by data-management` on the fresh count with nothing from the fixer in the loop, then adopt; afterwards the manifest carries an entry the diff reads as `judgment` or `coverage`, never `legacy`. A fresh count that differs from 253 of 586 is expected (the sandbox is in use) — the ratio is the claim, not the number.

## F-450 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-09-10 (tester — first live multi-tenant setup)
Severity: normal — all three were invisible on a single-tenant workspace and went live the moment a second tenant existed
What: three facts are stored at a scope that does not match what they describe. One class, three instances.
(a) `.gs-superadmin/CONVENTIONS.md` declares itself "Tenant-specific — fill in as patterns emerge" but lives at workspace scope, shared by every tenant. `jo-report-deps.mjs:188` hardcodes `join(wsDir, ".gs-superadmin", "CONVENTIONS.md")`, and `deps-report/SKILL.md:60` states both halves in one sentence — "the tenant's field-aliasing convention from the workspace's `.gs-superadmin/CONVENTIONS.md`". Fill it in for one tenant and the other's deps-report, email-report and audit silently adopt it. Nothing was lost this round only because the file is still the pristine template.
(b) Hard-required-flag exclusions (`--topic is required`, `ruleId or ruleName is required`, `--object-name … is required`) and the two server-side blocks are properties of the pinned CLI, not of a tenant, yet they live in `<slug>/_manifest.json`. The second tenant re-derived every one by live-failing three attempts per blocked domain, and the two tenants now disagree about what is physically enumerable.
(c) Scope limits are absent from the manifest entirely: `domains_indexed["journey-email-templates"]` carries the same six fields as a fully-enumerable domain, so any consumer reading the manifest sees the count as complete. The limitation exists only as prose in `skills/setup/references/index-scope-notes.md`.
Expected: one decision about where each kind of fact lives — per-tenant, per-workspace, or per-CLI-version — with readers deriving from that home rather than three independent placements.
Fix: 2026-09-15 (builder, Session C2 / FH-1; rulings, Bradley 2026-09-15 — (a) the workspace file is the default for every tenant and a `<slug>/CONVENTIONS.md` beside a tenant's KB overrides it for that tenant alone, the exception not the norm; (b) a plugin-shipped, version-stamped per-pin list; (c) the scope limit is DERIVED by `report` from that same table, never stamped per tenant) — one decision per KIND of fact, three homes. Class (not a registry key): a fact stored at the scope of the thing that happened to observe it — a per-CLI fact per tenant, a per-tenant fact per workspace — so a second tenant re-derives or inherits what is not its own. (a) `readAliasConvention` (jo-report-deps; tenant-deps and email-report read through it) resolves the tenant directory — the KB path's first segment under the workspace — and reads `<slug>/CONVENTIONS.md` when it EXISTS, the home whatever it contains (an unset or malformed declaration is reported against it, never completed from the workspace file: two files never read as one), else the workspace default; every result carries `home` and `path`, and the deps report header names the home ("the workspace CONVENTIONS.md, shared by every tenant" / "the tenant's own CONVENTIONS.md override"). The operating model's Build standards section is the canon; the template banner (which had promised "Tenant-specific" for a file every tenant read) and the audit, change-request, deprecate, deps-report and email-report prose paraphrase-plus-point at it. The scaffold writer still owns the workspace file; nobody auto-creates the tenant one. (b) doc-lib `CLI_PIN_FACTS`, keyed by catalog command `id` — NOT actionKey as the plan recommended: `list-source-fields` is the actionKey of two commands in two namespaces (measured) — stamped for the pin and applied only while the workspace catalog's cliVersion equals it (the ask-overrides precedent, self-retiring; under another pin the diff and the report say so and every sublist is ordinary work again). `domain-candidates.mjs diff` puts the four `re rules` sublists in a `notEnumerableBare` bucket BEFORE the record chain, each with the flag it needs and the runtime error; never undecided, never gating; a tenant exclusion or block recorded against one is `tenantRecord` on the entry plus one warning naming the lift verb, and is not counted among the decisions in force; a domain INDEXED from one stays visible as indexed with a contradiction warning; `pinFacts` rides the output. The `sources fields` pair stays on requiredEnumFlags (kickoff instruction; they declare `--type[enum]`). Measured over both real manifests, read-only: 4 `notEnumerableBare` each, all `tenantRecord: excluded` (inert), `undecidedCount` 0, `--require-decided` exit 0 on both, both files byte-identical before and after. (c) the same table carries `scope` for the three commands index-scope-notes names; `report` resolves each stamp's recorded `listCommand` through the catalog (the resolver upsert-batch's fork guard already used) and emits `domains.<d>.scope: { key, path, limit } | null` plus a top-level `pinFacts` (T-2 v4, additive, conformance-pinned); nothing stamped per tenant, no backfill, no `--scope` flag — both real manifests read `scope` on their two journey domains today (journey-email-templates and journey-surveys on each; the sandbox no longer carries a journey-data-designer domain and prod excluded that list as coverage). index-scope-notes.md is restructured into one `###` subsection per limited command, headed by the canonical path (= `scope.path`); the A-note on `jo data-designer list` is corrected (a membership signal over data-management, decided as a coverage exclusion, not a domain); check-doc-drift check 23 holds the table's scope ids and the subsections to each other both ways (mutants 23a–e all red: a heading respelled, a subsection with no entry, a subsection outside the section, the table's opener reshaped, the section heading renamed). Adoption tripwires: check-stale-facts FACT_CARRIERS pins the table's stamp to the catalog pin (mutation-proved on the real tree — stamp set to 1.0.8 → red naming CLI_PIN_FACTS; rig: stale stamp red by name with the other carriers green, missing stamp red as an unmatched carrier); test/domain-candidates.mjs holds every table id to the bundled catalog and reds a notEnumerableBare entry the catalog has started to declare (a dead entry). Same class, named as the kickoff asked: `connectors-chains` recorded `modifiedDateStr` on the sandbox and none on prod at the same pin — the cause IS in upsert-batch: `cn chains` at 1.0.9 emits `modifiedDateStr: ""` on every row (three captured pages in the workspace, July, August and September, all four rows blank on each), and the value predicate counted a blank as a resolved date, so the sandbox stored `""` on all four chains (newerThan("", "") is false — never a change, and report counted them as dated) while prod's operator, seeing blanks, recorded none. Fixed: a blank string is present-but-valueless (stored null, `datelessEntries` counts it; `datePresentRows` still counts the path), a full list blank on EVERY row warns once with the `--no-date-field --allow-redate` remedy (present-but-NULL rows stay warning-free — F-392's ruling stands, and the fixture pins the mixed case), and a blank stored before the rule is cleared on the next upsert (`blankDatesCleared`). Prod's recording is the right one; the sandbox's redate is the tester's (VALIDATION § F-450 / F-452, step 4). ## F-451 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-09-10 (tester — first live multi-tenant setup)
Severity: normal — silently removes assets from change detection; the KB looks current and is not
What: on the sandbox tenant, 557 of 1,180 `journey-email-templates` entries carry no `modified_date` and 560 carry no `name` — the entries registered by the list-invisible recovery path. /refresh detects change by comparing dates, so those entries have nothing to compare and are permanently invisible to staleness: documented once in July, never flagged again. The missing `name` means inventory-side name lookups return null for them.
The reach is wider than the recovery path, and this is the part that needs answering before a fix is scoped. Entries with no `modified_date`:

    report                    1696 (sandbox) / 1754 (prod)
    journey-email-templates    557 (sandbox)
    journey-data-designer       69 (sandbox)
    connectors-chains            4 (sandbox)

The whole `report` domain is dateless on both tenants. The manifest supports an explicit-none `dateField`, so this may be a handled state with a documented fallback — or it may mean the entire report inventory sits outside change detection.
Expected: either a documented fallback /refresh applies to dateless entries, or an honest statement in the refresh report naming what it could not check — never silence.
Fix: 2026-09-15 (builder, Session C1 / RP-3; ruled 2026-09-11, Bradley: honest statement now, fingerprint-based staleness is #12) — `report` emits per domain (`domains.<d>`) `changeDetection: "date" | "none" | "unrecorded"` and `datelessEntries`: `date` = a modified-date field is recorded on the stamp; `none` = recorded-none (`dateField: null`) — the whole domain sits outside change detection; `unrecorded` = a legacy stamp with no `dateField` key, a bare-string stamp, or no stamp at all (T-2's tri-state, never read as "none"); `datelessEntries` counts entries with no stored `modified_date` whatever the state, which under `date` are exactly the rows the comparison can never flag (the recovery-path registrations). The three measured shapes each have a fixture domain (recorded-none; a recorded field under which every row is null; a healthy dated domain) plus the legacy no-key stamp. Prose: refresh step 1 keeps the report's `domains` block and step 4's report ends with a `Not checked for change this run:` block — one line per `none` domain (whole domain outside detection), per `unrecorded` domain (field recorded this run, detection starts next refresh), and per `date` domain with `datelessEntries > 0` (n of t rows carry no date) — or the single word `none`, never omitted. "Unchanged" now says what it could see. Class: the refresh report's "Unchanged: Z" asserted "no change" from a date comparison for rows that carry no date to compare. Measured locally over both real manifests (read-only), reproducing the bus counts: prod `report` domain 1754 dateless under `none`, five recorded-none domains totalling 2362 of 5076; the sandbox `journey-email-templates` 557 dateless under a recorded field (`date`), its `report` domain 1696 under `none`, and its `report-objects` legacy stamp reads `unrecorded` (588 dateless, all pending). Rides 0.40.0.
Class: outcome-from-proxy
Judge: the tester's `report` over both real manifests reproducing those counts (prod report 1754 under `none`; sandbox templates 557 under `date`), and the refresh walk's report carrying the `Not checked for change this run:` block naming them — a refresh report that ends at "Unchanged" with those domains unnamed REOPENS this entry.
Sibling sweep: outcome-from-proxy recipe, shared with F-455's line above — the one sibling site NAMED and not closed is `upsert-batch`'s `unchanged` count, which folds dateless rows in; the refresh report now states the same fact from `report`'s per-domain `datelessEntries`, so nothing is silent, and a qualified upsert field is banked for the next round rather than changed without a ruling. Cost: minutes.

## F-453 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-09-10 (tester — first live multi-tenant setup)
Severity: polish — correct fail-closed behaviour; the cost is friction and an undocumented workaround
What: a Phase 4 loop that built its `gs-admin` subcommand from a shell variable was refused by the mutation guard, which cannot verify a command it cannot read. The refusal is correct. But it fired on a read-only enumeration loop during setup, and the resolution — spell the subcommands literally — appears nowhere in the skills; the session derived it. A user without that instinct is stuck on a correct refusal with no stated remedy.
Expected: wherever the skills instruct building a list of commands to run, the literal-spelling requirement is stated, so the guard's refusal is anticipated rather than debugged.

Amended 2026-09-10 (tester, same round) — the What above is WRONG on its central claim, and the correction changes the finding. The remedy does not "appear nowhere in the skills": `templates/operating-model.md:135` states it directly — "**Spell subcommands literally**: the mutation guard checks command *text*, so a subcommand hidden in a shell variable (`gs-admin --json $c` in a loop) can't be verified and triggers approval prompts even for reads" — anticipating this exact case, including that it fires on reads. The session that hit the refusal had read that file in full roughly forty minutes earlier, then wrote the variable-built loop anyway.
So this is not a documentation gap, and a second copy of the rule would fix nothing. It is a rung-3 statement (AGENTS.md's shared-prose table: a session-global doc every session reads) that did not fire at the moment of composition. That table's own remedy is to move the rule down a rung: the guard already refuses at exactly the right instant and is the only thing present at that instant, but its refusal message does not name the remedy. Stating "spell the domain/group/command words literally; variables belong in flag values and paths" in the refusal turns a correct-but-opaque block into a self-resolving one, at rung 1. Severity unchanged; what changes is the target — the guard's message, not the docs.
Fix: 2026-09-16 (builder, Session D / DC-2) — the guard's repeat-offense ASK on a shell-variable subcommand now carries the remedy its first-offense DENY already named: "To avoid the prompt, rewrite with the domain/group/command words spelled literally — variables belong in flag values and paths — and retry: a literal read-only command runs without any prompt" (hooks/gs-admin-guard.mjs, the varAskPart string; the deny text is unchanged). Class behind the instance: a two-branch message where only one branch named the remedy — the rung-1 site was present at the moment of composition and said "approve only if you know what it expands to", never how to not need the prompt. No skill prose added, per the amendment's own ruling (a second copy of operating-model.md's "Spell subcommands literally" would fix nothing). Fixture: guard-fixtures' repeat path gains a check pinning /spelled literally/ and "flag values and paths" on the ASK; mutation-proved by running the suite over the pre-fix hook (git stash of the hook alone): the new check is the only red. The F-363 bound arm (50 variable subcommands + 100 tenant dirs) re-measured with the longer ask — still under the bound (its measured line prints the bytes). ## F-455 — VERIFIED
Reported: 2026-09-10 (tester — first live multi-tenant setup, during a shallow crawl with per-domain deep ingests)
Severity: normal — no stored data is wrong and no stub misrepresents itself; what is wrong is the completion signal the user is asked to act on, and downstream decisions (rebuilding relationship maps, trusting a deps-report answer) rest on it
What: `manifest.mjs report` is the deterministic account of KB state, and its schema carries no depth at all. A metadata stub and a full describe are both counted as `documented`, in `byStatus` and in every `byDomain` row, so the report cannot distinguish a documented domain from an ingested one:

    "byStatus": { "documented": 5076 }
    "byDomain": { "rules-engine": { "documented": 497 },
                  "report": { "documented": 1754 }, ... }

Zero pending, zero stale, everything "documented" — while a tally of the `depth` field the manifest already stores, taken at 2026-09-10 17:08 local, read 1381 full against 3695 stubs across the same 5076 entries, `crawl_mode` shallow.
Consequence observed live: after one domain's deep ingest completed, the user was told the deep crawl was finished and that every domain was at full depth except the list-only ones and `journey-email-templates`. Eight further domains were entirely stubs at that moment, and a further domain's deep ingest began afterwards. This was not a careless relay — the report contains no fact that could have contradicted the claim, so the model had nothing to check itself against and the user had nothing to check the model against.
Note the same conflation is deliberate and correct elsewhere: Phase 6's precondition counts stubs as documented on purpose, because a stub never blocks synthesis. The defect is that the one mechanical statement of state offers no depth anywhere, so a human-facing completion claim cannot be grounded in it.
Second, smaller point found while measuring this: the manifest is rewritten continuously during a run, so a tally taken mid-ingest is a snapshot of a moving target and will disagree with one taken a minute later. A completeness check is only meaningful at a quiescent point. (The reporter made exactly this mistake while drafting the entry — a mid-run sample showed one asset short of a domain's full ingest, which the next read showed complete.)
Expected: depth is part of the mechanical account, not something a reader reconstructs. `report` (or a sibling verb) carries a per-domain full/stub/list-only breakdown derived from the `depth` the manifest already stores, with list-only domains reported complete by definition rather than as stubs, so the three states stay distinguishable. And every place a skill states that documentation is complete, or that a domain is fully ingested, derives that statement from the script's output rather than from its own narrative — one invocation, quoted, at a point where nothing is still writing.
Fix: 2026-09-15 (builder, Session C1 / RP-1) — `manifest.mjs report` carries `byDepth` = { full, metadata, listOnly, unrecorded } over DOCUMENTED entries, in total and per domain under a new `domains.<d>` row (ruling, Bradley 2026-09-15: four states, per-domain block — `unrecorded` is NOT folded into `metadata`, because a stub under a domain with no describe recording is the F-346 false-complete class, and nothing new goes inside a `byDomain` row because describe-batch's progress probe sums those). A metadata stub is bucketed by its DOMAIN's recorded describe state through ONE helper (`describeStateOf`) the stub banner now shares, so the report and the docs on disk say the same three things; a documented entry with no depth at all (a pre-depth-field doc, never a stub) counts as full — the stub verb's own never-downgrade rule. Class: the report field `documented` asserted completeness from a status that describes doc EXISTENCE, not depth — every skill sentence about completeness was derived from that proxy or from the run's own narrative. Prose: setup Phase 5 closes on ONE quoted `report` at a quiescent point (`byDepth` + `domains.<d>.byDepth`; "fully ingested" = `metadata: 0` and `unrecorded: 0` with no pending/stale — never a tally taken mid-batch), the `--deep` relay quotes the same row, Phase 6's precondition reads that report's `byStatus` (stubs still count as documented, deliberately), the final report gains a `Depth:` line and a `Not complete:` line, and document-mechanics §4's shapes derive from it (new "Completeness unknown" line for unrecorded stubs). Contract: report's output is now T-2's `GsReport` (manifest.mjs header, v3, additive) pinned by test/contract-conformance.mjs (exact key sets, byDomain numbers-only). Measured locally over both real manifests (read-only): prod reads 6 domains listOnly (722 entries) and 0 metadata / 0 unrecorded — every `none` domain listOnly, none as metadata; the sandbox reads 5 domains unrecorded (its five legacy stamps) and 0 listOnly. Fixtures: test/manifest-ops.mjs "c1" section (35 arms over a manifest carrying all four states + a pre-depth doc; 27 red against the pre-fix script, the rest rig setup and controls). Version 0.40.0. Pick up: /reload-plugins.
Class: outcome-from-proxy
Judge: (1) the T-2 v3 conformance pin (key sets re-derived from the typedef, never imported); (2) independent of the fixer: the tester runs `report` over BOTH real manifests in the consumer workspace and holds the output to the claims above — every list-only domain of prod reads listOnly, none reads metadata; the sandbox's five legacy stamps read unrecorded — then walks setup once and reads the Phase 5 close / final report quoting `byDepth` from one invocation. A skill relay that states completeness from anything but that quoted report REOPENS this entry.
Sibling sweep: outcome-from-proxy recipe — one read per outcome-writing site. manifest.mjs summary fields: `report.byStatus.documented` (this entry — qualified by `byDepth`), `remove.docPaths` (F-459 — qualified by `docPathsUnknown`), `upsert-batch.unchanged` (NAMED, not closed: it counts rows whose stored and incoming dates are both null as "unchanged" — the same fact F-451's `datelessEntries` now states one layer down in `report`, which the refresh report names; a qualified field on the upsert summary is the one remaining site, banked for C2 / #12 rather than changed without a ruling), `stub.stubbed` / `mark.status` / `next.count` / `crawl` / `reconcile-docs` (signal = the write this verb just made, unit = the same entry: no mismatch). Skills: `grep -rn -i "fully ingested\|deep crawl\|is complete\|up to date\|fully documented" skills templates` — every remaining hit is either the crawl-mode question text (a promise about the mechanism, not a state claim) or a sentence that now quotes the report. Cost: minutes.
